docs.text: Driver TMC5160 Driver ¶ A C++20 driver for the TMC5160 and TMC5160A stepper motor controller and driver. It starts the chip safely, moves the motor in physical units, and refuses the register writes that can burn out a motor or a bridge, on any MCU, over SPI or UART. Quickstart API guide Source on GitHub The driver has no platform code. You give it a small class that brings the bus up and moves bytes; it does the rest: the start-up sequence, the datagram framing and CRC, the current arithmetic, the ramp registers, the guards and the timeouts. Nothing here has run on a chip yet: it is tested against an independent model of the TMC5160 (see Testing and CI ). Stepper motor controller and driver TMC5160 / TMC5160A Analog Devices (Trinamic) Function Ramp generator, sequencer with a 256-entry microstep table, StealthChop2, SpreadCycle, StallGuard2, CoolStep, DcStep, encoder input, gate drivers for two external MOSFET bridges Interface SPI mode 3 (also a daisy chain), or single wire UART with CRC-8 (also several nodes); STEP/DIR mode Power Motor supply 10 V to 55 V, I/O supply 3.0 V to 5.25 V, sense threshold 325 mV Package TQFP-48 with exposed pad (7 x 7 mm); QFN-WA variant What you get ¶ One object per chip. TMC5160<YourPort> takes a reference to your port and does no I/O until EnsureInitialized() . See API guide . A current that cannot exceed the motor. You declare the motor and the sense resistor; every register is derived from them. See Current and limits . A guard for every dangerous write. What the driver refuses, and the explicit acknowledgement that lifts a guard for one call. See Guards and acknowledgements . Errors you can act on. Every call returns Result<T> with an Error such as Bus , Timeout , Refused or UnexpectedReset . See API guide . Both buses. SPI and UART ports, daisy chains and multi-node lines, STEP/DIR mode. See SPI protocol and UART protocol . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI. The host tests build with -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti . See Contract . Where the datasheet is unclear, a decision. Fifty ambiguities are listed with the reading the driver takes. See Ambiguities . Datasheet ¶ Document Revision Get it Datasheet: TMC5160 / TMC5160A Datasheet (Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS) 1.18, 2023-03-01 vendor page Written against these revisions; the SHA-256 of each file is in docs/datasheets.yml . Where each part of the driver is in the datasheet: Datasheet map . Where to go next ¶ Quickstart Wire the chip, write the port, declare the motor and move it in about 20 lines. Hardware Pins, bus settings, timing and power. Guards and acknowledgements What is refused, why, and how to lift a guard for one call. Contract What the driver promises, what it needs, threading and errors. API guide Start, set the current, move, tune and diagnose, task by task. Porting Implement the SPI or UART port for your MCU.

docs.text: Ambiguities ¶ Where the datasheet is unclear or contradicts itself, the reading the driver takes, and how the tests cover the other one. Forty-nine questions came up while reading the datasheet (revision 1.18). Each has a decision, and the decision is tested against the model. A knob is a setting of the chip model in tests/mock_tmc5160.hpp ( Knobs ) or of the bus ( Faults ) that makes the model behave the other way, so a test can run the driver against each reading. Where a row says "guard", the decision is the driver's alone (a limit it enforces) and the chip has nothing to vary; the row names the test. Nothing here was checked on a chip: confirming each reading on hardware is open work. Id Question Decision Knob or test A1 SPI clock polarity and phase Mode 3 (page 25 says "usually referred to as SPI MODE 3") Faults::spi_mode : the model frames mode 3 only A2 Maximum SCK 4 MHz internal clock, fCLK / 2 less 10 percent external Faults::sck_hz A3 Status byte age One transfer old; never acted on in the same call Knobs::status_lag A4 Reading a write-only register Never read; Refused ; the shadow answers Knobs::wo_read_mode (zeros, last value, garbage) A5 Write echo Used only by Verify::Echo Knobs::echo_writes A6 Microstep table alignment Bit n is the increment into entry n Knobs::lut_literal_reading A7 MSCURACT field order As documented, sign-extend 9 bits Knobs::mscuract_swap A8 Reset defaults depend on OTP Documented defaults; docs.text: API guide ¶ The driver's API by task, with code that compiles: start, set the current, move, tune, watch, handle errors and stop. The shape of the API ¶ Group Calls Page Lifecycle EnsureInitialized() , IsInitialized() , Enable() , Disable() , Deinitialize() below Current SetCurrent() and the declared motor Current and limits Motion MoveTo() , MoveBy() , RunVelocity() , Stop() , SetRamp() , PositionReached() Motion Chopper SetChopper() , SetStealthChop() , SetThresholds() Chopper Load SetStallGuard() , SetStopOnStall() , ReleaseStall() , CoolStep StallGuard and CoolStep Status Service() , ReadRampStatus() , ClearFaults() Diagnostics and status Guards Ack , Verify Guards Every call that touches the chip returns Result<T> : check ok() (or the bool conversion) and read value , or read error . Result is [[nodiscard]] , so an unchecked call is a compiler warning. Start, enable, stop ¶ // Start, enable, stop. Every call returns a Result: check it. tmc5160 :: Error RunAndStop ( Motor & motor ) { if ( auto r = motor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // writes every register; the driver stays off return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . Enable (); ! r ) { // refuses after a chip reset or a driver fault return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . RunVelocity ( 50'000 ); ! r ) { // VMAX in the chip's own units, signed return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . Stop ( tmc5160 :: StopKind :: Ramp ); ! r ) { // decelerate with the programmed ramp return r . error ; } return motor . Disable (). error ; // DRV_ENN inactive; the motor is not held } The constructor stores the port and the configuration and does no I/O. EnsureInitialized() is the one way to start the chip; it leaves the power stage off. Enable() switches it on, and refuses after a chip reset or a driver fault. Config{} is not valid: build one with MakeConfig() from the motor and the sense resistor ( Configuration ). Once EnsureInitialized() has succeeded it returns Ok at once with no I/O. After a failure the driver stays uninitialised and the next call starts again. Before it succeeds every call returns NotInitialized and sends nothing. Set the current ¶ // The current is always checked against the declared motor and the sense resistor. tmc5160 :: Error SetCurrents ( Motor & motor ) { const auto plan = motor . SetCurrent ( 800 , 240 ); // run and hold, mA rms if ( ! plan ) { return plan . error ; // LimitExceeded: above the motor or the 5 % ceiling, or below one CS step } // `plan.value` holds GLOBALSCALER, IRUN, IHOLD and the realised currents. return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; } Move ¶ // Position mode: the ramp generator moves to XTARGET. Poll PositionReached(). tmc5160 :: Error GoTo ( Motor & motor , int32_t target ) { if ( auto r = motor . MoveTo ( target ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < 1000 ; ++ i ) { // bounded: the caller decides how long a move may take const auto done = motor . PositionReached (); if ( ! done ) { return done . error ; } if ( done . value ) { return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; } } return tmc5160 :: Error :: Timeout ; } Quiet running and stall detection ¶ // StealthChop below a velocity, SpreadCycle above it. tmc5160 :: Error QuietMotor ( Motor & motor ) { tmc5160 :: StealthChop stealth ; stealth . enable = true ; if ( auto r = motor . SetStealthChop ( stealth ); ! r ) { // waits the automatic tuning time at standstill return r . error ; } return motor . SetThresholds ( tmc5160 :: Thresholds {. pwm = 500 }) . error ; // TSTEP above 500 is StealthChop } // StallGuard2 with a stop on stall. The motor stays stopped until ReleaseStall(). tmc5160 :: Error SensorlessStop ( Motor & motor ) { if ( auto r = motor . SetThresholds ( tmc5160 :: Thresholds {. cool = 200'000 }); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . SetStallGuard ( tmc5160 :: StallGuard {. threshold = 4 , . filter = true }); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . SetStopOnStall ( true ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } const auto ramp = motor . ReadRampStatus (); if ( ramp && ramp . value . event_stop_stall ) { return motor . ReleaseStall (). error ; // clear the event: the motor may move again } return ramp . error ; } Watch the chip ¶ // A periodic service call: one batch read, the events decoded and the latched ones cleared. tmc5160 :: Error ServiceLoop ( Motor & motor ) { const auto events = motor . Service (); if ( ! events ) { return events . error ; // UnexpectedReset: write-only registers are lost, Enable() refuses } if ( events . value . driver . over_temp || events . value . driver . s2g_a || events . value . driver . s2g_b ) { return tmc5160 :: Error :: DeviceFault ; } return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; } Dangerous writes ¶ // A guarded write: IHOLD above IRUN is refused unless the call acknowledges it. tmc5160 :: Error HoldAboveRun ( Motor & motor ) { tmc5160 :: Config c = motor . GetConfig (); c . current . hold_ma = c . current . run_ma + 100 ; const auto refused = motor . SetCurrent ( c . current . run_ma , c . current . hold_ma ); return refused . error ; // Refused: no tmc5160::Ack::HoldAboveRun in the configuration } Handle errors ¶ // What each error asks of the application. const char * Advice ( tmc5160 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case tmc5160 :: Error :: Bus : case tmc5160 :: Error :: Timeout : case tmc5160 :: Error :: Crc : return "retry the read; a write is not retried: look at the wiring" ; // reads are retried twice case tmc5160 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset : return "the chip lost its registers: EnsureInitialized() again" ; case tmc5160 :: Error :: DeviceFault : return "short or overtemperature: remove the cause, then ClearFaults()" ; case tmc5160 :: Error :: Refused : case tmc5160 :: Error :: LimitExceeded : return "the guard stopped an unsafe request: change the request" ; default : return "see the error table" ; } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring Error::Timeout No UART reply, or a bounded wait ran out Check the single wire, the node address and the baud rate Error::Crc A UART reply was corrupted Check the wire and grounding; reads are retried twice, writes never Error::UnexpectedReset The chip reset: write-only registers are lost EnsureInitialized() again Error::DeviceFault Short or overtemperature Remove the cause, then ClearFaults() Error::Refused A guard stopped the call Change the request, or acknowledge the risk in the configuration Error::LimitExceeded Above the motor, the board or the ramp limit Change the request Error::ModeMismatch The strap or the bus does not match Config::mode Fix the strap or the configuration Error::VerifyFailed A write-back or interface-counter check failed Rewrite with EnsureInitialized() ; check the wire Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. tmc5160::ToString() names an error for a log. Stop ¶ // Release the driver: the chip is quiesced and every later call returns NotInitialized. tmc5160 :: Error Shutdown ( Motor & motor ) { return motor . Deinitialize (). error ; } After Deinitialize() the chip is quiesced and every call returns NotInitialized until the next EnsureInitialized() . Next: Configuration .

SetStallGuard ( tmc5160 :: StallGuard {. threshold = 4 , . filter = true }); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . SetStopOnStall ( true ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } const auto ramp = motor . ReadRampStatus (); if ( ramp && ramp . value . event_stop_stall ) { return motor . ReleaseStall (). error ; // clear the event: the motor may move again } return ramp . error ; }
docs.title: Quiet running and stall detection

docs.text: // A periodic service call: one batch read, the events decoded and the latched ones cleared. tmc5160 :: Error ServiceLoop ( Motor & motor ) { const auto events = motor . Service (); if ( ! events ) { return events . error ; // UnexpectedReset: write-only registers are lost, Enable() refuses } if ( events . value . driver . over_temp || events . value . driver . s2g_a || events . value . driver . s2g_b ) { return tmc5160 :: Error :: DeviceFault ; } return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; }
docs.title: Watch the chip

docs.text: // A guarded write: IHOLD above IRUN is refused unless the call acknowledges it. tmc5160 :: Error HoldAboveRun ( Motor & motor ) { tmc5160 :: Config c = motor . GetConfig (); c . current . hold_ma = c . current . run_ma + 100 ; const auto refused = motor . SetCurrent ( c . current . run_ma , c . current . hold_ma ); return refused . error ; // Refused: no tmc5160::Ack::HoldAboveRun in the configuration }
docs.title: Dangerous writes

docs.text: // What each error asks of the application. const char * Advice ( tmc5160 :: Error e ) { switch ( e ) { case tmc5160 :: Error :: Bus : case tmc5160 :: Error :: Timeout : case tmc5160 :: Error :: Crc : return "retry the read; a write is not retried: look at the wiring" ; // reads are retried twice case tmc5160 :: Error :: UnexpectedReset : return "the chip lost its registers: EnsureInitialized() again" ; case tmc5160 :: Error :: DeviceFault : return "short or overtemperature: remove the cause, then ClearFaults()" ; case tmc5160 :: Error :: Refused : case tmc5160 :: Error :: LimitExceeded : return "the guard stopped an unsafe request: change the request" ; default : return "see the error table" ; } } Signal Meaning What to do Error::Bus The port failed a transfer or the bus bring-up Check the port and the wiring Error::Timeout No UART reply, or a bounded wait ran out Check the single wire, the node address and the baud rate Error::Crc A UART reply was corrupted Check the wire and grounding; reads are retried twice, writes never Error::UnexpectedReset The chip reset: write-only registers are lost EnsureInitialized() again Error::DeviceFault Short or overtemperature Remove the cause, then ClearFaults() Error::Refused A guard stopped the call Change the request, or acknowledge the risk in the configuration Error::LimitExceeded Above the motor, the board or the ramp limit Change the request Error::ModeMismatch The strap or the bus does not match Config::mode Fix the strap or the configuration Error::VerifyFailed A write-back or interface-counter check failed Rewrite with EnsureInitialized() ; check the wire Every value, with the calls that return it, is on the Contract page. tmc5160::ToString() names an error for a log.
docs.title: Handle errors

docs.text: // Release the driver: the chip is quiesced and every later call returns NotInitialized. tmc5160 :: Error Shutdown ( Motor & motor ) { return motor . Deinitialize (). error ; } After Deinitialize() the chip is quiesced and every call returns NotInitialized until the next EnsureInitialized() . Next: Configuration .

docs.text: Architecture ¶ How the driver is built: three layers, one of them yours, and what happens in each when you move the motor. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Features, control interfaces and key concepts: 1 Principles of Operation, p. 5 Initialization examples: 23.1 Initialization Examples, p. 116 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The layers, one of them yours Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your application calls one object, whose public calls are listed from the umbrella header in inc/. The core turns each call into register reads and writes and hands them to the port contract (the CRTP base in inc/*_interface.hpp), which forwards them, at compile time, to the hooks of the port class you write; your port moves the bytes on the bus. The notes on the right say which layers stay the same on every MCU and which one you write. A library without a port contract has only the first two layers. Drawn from: inc/tmc5160.hpp public calls ; inc/tmc5160_spi_interface.hpp SpiInterface ; figure module docs/diagrams/figures/driver-layers.py . Layers ¶ Layer Files Owns Core inc/tmc5160.hpp , src/tmc5160.ipp Lifecycle, guards, motion, status, framing of both buses, errors Types and registers inc/tmc5160_types.hpp , inc/tmc5160_registers.hpp , inc/tmc5160_status.hpp Error , Result<T> , Config and its parts; the register table; decoded status Units inc/tmc5160_units.hpp Pure integer helpers: the current plan, ramp conversions, the encoder scale Helpers inc/tmc5160_detail.hpp Typed integer literals, the exact hook probes, CRC-8, field packing Port contracts inc/tmc5160_spi_interface.hpp , inc/tmc5160_uart_interface.hpp The CRTP bases, the concepts, the bus requirements Platform port Your class Bus bring-up and byte transfers, optionally delays, GPIO, the clock and logging Kconfig layer inc/tmc5160_kconfig.hpp Optional: a Config from ESP-IDF menuconfig One call through the layers ¶ sequenceDiagram participant App as Your code participant Core as TMC5160<Port> participant Port as Your port App->>Core: SetCurrent(800, 240) Note over Core: PlanCurrent: ceiling, sense bound, scaler Core->>Port: Transfer(write GLOBALSCALER) Port-->>Core: true, status byte Note over Core: reset flag? return UnexpectedReset Core->>Port: Transfer(write IHOLD_IRUN) Port-->>Core: true, status byte Core-->>App: Result<CurrentPlan> Design choices ¶ CRTP, not virtual functions. The port is a template parameter constrained by the SpiPort or UartPort concept, so every call is resolved at compile time and a missing hook is a compile error that names it. One bus per object. The base class decides the bus; the framing code is if constexpr on it, so a UART port carries no SPI code. A shadow of the write-only registers. Most TMC5160 registers cannot be read. The driver writes whole 32-bit words from a write-through shadow and never reads them back; this also makes UnexpectedReset detectable and recoverable. The configuration is the source of truth. Every setter builds the next Config , validates it, writes the affected registers and only then stores it, so a failed call leaves the stored configuration as it was. Guards in one place. Every dangerous write goes through one guard function that knows the acknowledgements. Optional hooks by requires . DelayUs , GpioSet , GpioGet , SckHz and Log are detected in one place. No I/O in the constructor. Construction cannot fail, so the driver can be a static or a member of a handler. One error type. Result<T> carries a value and an Error ; nothing throws and nothing returns a bare bool . No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no printf . The driver is a header-only template with no mutable static state. docs.text: StealthChop and SpreadCycle ¶ The two chopper modes, the thresholds that switch between them and the sequencing of StealthChop's automatic tuning. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Velocity dependent control: 6.2 Velocity Dependent Driver Feature Control Register Set, p. 38 Motor driver registers: 6.5 Motor Driver Registers, p. 47 Chopper configuration: 6.5 Motor Driver Registers, p. 51 StealthChop2 and automatic tuning: 7 StealthChop, p. 57 StealthChop and SpreadCycle combined: 7.5 Combine StealthChop and SpreadCycle, p. 64 Freewheeling and passive braking: 7.7 Freewheeling and Passive Braking, p. 66 SpreadCycle and classic chopper: 8 SpreadCycle and Classic Chopper, p. 68 Velocity based mode control: 10 Velocity Based Mode Control, p. 76 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . SpreadCycle and the classic chopper ¶ SetChopper() writes CHOPCONF from Chopper : the chopper mode, TOFF, TBL, hysteresis, the microstep resolution and the high-velocity options. TOFF 0 switches the driver off; the driver only writes it through Disable() . toff 1 needs tbl 2 or more, and the effective hysteresis sum may not exceed 16 (section 8.1, page 69). The reset value of CHOPCONF is 0x10410150 and the driver always writes the whole word from its shadow. StealthChop2 ¶ SetStealthChop() writes PWMCONF and the enable bit. StealthChop may only be switched on at standstill with IHOLD equal to IRUN: the driver checks standstill as Enable() does ( Busy otherwise), writes IHOLD = IRUN, enables the mode, waits the automatic tuning time (AT#1, at most 130 ms plus a margin) with bounded DelayUs() calls, then restores the hold current. The second tuning step (AT#2) is a motion at 60 to 300 RPM that the application performs; ReadStealthChopState() returns PWM_SCALE and PWM_AUTO to judge it. // StealthChop below a velocity, SpreadCycle above it. tmc5160 :: Error QuietMotor ( Motor & motor ) { tmc5160 :: StealthChop stealth ; stealth . enable = true ; if ( auto r = motor . SetStealthChop ( stealth ); ! r ) { // waits the automatic tuning time at standstill return r . error ; } return motor . SetThresholds ( tmc5160 :: Thresholds {. pwm = 500 }) . error ; // TSTEP above 500 is StealthChop } With autoscale on, IRUN must be at least 8, TPOWERDOWN at least 2, and when the coil resistance is declared the run current must be above the lower limit tBLANK * fPWM * VM / Rcoil (section 7.3, page 62), otherwise Refused . Changing GLOBALSCALER or the supply invalidates the tuning (page 59). A hard stop of the switch or stall stop ( Switches::soft_stop false) with StealthChop on can cause a large overcurrent for tens of milliseconds, so it needs Ack::HardStopWithStealthChop ; the Stop() kinds are ramps and need none. Thresholds ¶ Register Field Meaning TPWMTHRS Thresholds::pwm StealthChop below this velocity (TSTEP above it), SpreadCycle above TCOOLTHRS Thresholds::cool CoolStep and the stall output above this velocity THIGH Thresholds::high The high-velocity chopper mode above this velocity TSTEP is a time, so a larger threshold value means a lower velocity. The ordering rule is TPWMTHRS at least TCOOLTHRS at least THIGH where non-zero (section 10, page 76). Freewheeling and passive braking ¶ StealthChop::freewheel chooses the standstill mode when IHOLD is 0 (section 7.7, page 66); the driver allows it only with IHOLD 0 and StealthChop on. Not provided ¶ PWM_OFS and PWM_GRAD estimate helpers (section 7.4, page 63) are not implemented; the caller sets the values in StealthChop::ofs and grad , or relies on the automatic tuning.

docs.text: Configuration ¶ Every field of tmc5160::Config , how a configuration is built and checked, and the optional Kconfig layer. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Register map and reset values: 6 Register Mapping, p. 31 General configuration registers: 6.1 General Configuration Registers, p. 32 Quick configuration guide: 22 Quick Configuration Guide, p. 111 Clock oscillator and input: 26 Clock Oscillator and Input, p. 119 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Start from the motor ¶ Config{} holds the chip's reset values, but it is not a usable configuration : it declares no motor and no sense resistor, and the driver derives every current register from those two. Validate(Config{}) returns InvalidArgument . Build a configuration with MakeConfig(motor, board) , which sets the run current to 85 percent of the motor's ceiling and the hold current to 30 percent of that, then change fields: tmc5160 :: Config StealthConfig () { tmc5160 :: Config c = tmc5160 :: MakeConfig ( tmc5160 :: Motor {. rated_rms_ma = 1500 , . coil_resistance_mohm = 2000 }, tmc5160 :: Board {. rsense_mohm = 75 , . supply_mv = 24'000 }); c . current . run_ma = 1000 ; // the run current in mA rms: never above the declared motor c . current . hold_ma = 300 ; // the hold current c . chopper . mres = tmc5160 :: Microsteps :: M16 ; // 16 microsteps per full step c . stealth . enable = true ; return c ; // tmc5160::Validate(c) checks it without the chip } tmc5160 :: Error StartStealth ( MyPort & port ) { static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > motor ( port , StealthConfig ()); // stored, no I/O return motor . EnsureInitialized () . error ; // InvalidArgument if a value is out of range or above the motor } Fields ¶ Field Default Meaning Registers mode MotionController MotionController or StepDir ; must match the SD_MODE strap GCONF, IOIN clock internal 12 MHz external and hz (4 to 18 MHz) all time and velocity values motor none rated_rms_ma , max_rms_ma , coil_resistance_mohm , fullsteps_per_rev the current ceiling board none rsense_mohm , supply_mv (10 000 to 55 000), supply_max_mv GLOBALSCALER, guards max_velocity_reg 0 Optional ceiling for VMAX VMAX include_tolerance true Reduce the ceiling by the 5 percent full-scale tolerance current plan current from MakeConfig() run_ma , hold_ma GLOBALSCALER, IHOLD_IRUN standstill datasheet hold_delay , power_down_delay , fast_standstill IHOLD_IRUN, TPOWERDOWN, GCONF chopper SpreadCycle, TOFF 3 mode, TOFF, TBL, hysteresis, mres , high-velocity options CHOPCONF stealth off enable, autoscale, autograd, frequency, regulation, limits, offsets, freewheel PWMCONF, GCONF thresholds 0 pwm , cool , high , small_hysteresis TPWMTHRS, TCOOLTHRS, THIGH cool , stall , dcstep off CoolStep, StallGuard2, DcStep COOLCONF, DCCTRL, VDCMIN bridge , protection not declared Gate-driver and short-protection values, written only when declared DRV_CONF, SHORT_CONF flags , diag off General flags; DIAG outputs GCONF ramp datasheet quick start The six-point ramp VSTART to TZEROWAIT switches off Reference switches and stop behaviour SW_MODE encoder not declared ENCMODE, ENC_CONST, deviation ENCMODE and following custom_table , table default table A custom microstep table MSLUT, MSLUTSEL, MSLUTSTART uart node 0, 115200 baud node, send_delay , multi_node , baud NODECONF spi chain of 1 chain_length , chain_index transfer length verify None The check EnsureInitialized() applies to its writes ack none Acknowledgements that lift guards ( Guards ) begin_enabled false Leave the driver enabled after EnsureInitialized() ; a motor that is still turning (or in its TZEROWAIT pause) makes the start-up fail with Busy , bridge off CHOPCONF.TOFF TOFF defaults to 3 where the chip's reset value is 0 (off): the chip's CHOPCONF reset word is 0x10410150 , but the driver writes TOFF only in Enable() , so a configured chopper never runs before you ask for it. Validation ¶ Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() calls it before any I/O. It returns InvalidArgument when a field is out of range, the motor or the sense resistor is missing, a current is above the motor's ceiling, or a combination breaks a guard. CheckedConfig runs it at build time: constexpr CheckedConfig kBoard{MakeConfig(...)} does not compile when the configuration is invalid. Kconfig ¶ Under ESP-IDF, idf.py menuconfig shows TMC5160 stepper driver when the driver is a component of the project ( Installation ); the menu is _config/Kconfig . The options reach the code only through inc/tmc5160_kconfig.hpp , never through a driver signature: tmc5160 :: Error StartFromMenuconfig ( MyPort & port ) { static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > motor ( port , tmc5160 :: KconfigDefaults ()); return motor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } Option Default Config field CONFIG_TMC5160_MOTOR_RATED_MA 1000 motor.rated_rms_ma CONFIG_TMC5160_MOTOR_MAX_MA 0 motor.max_rms_ma CONFIG_TMC5160_RSENSE_MOHM 100 board.rsense_mohm CONFIG_TMC5160_SUPPLY_MV 24000 board.supply_mv CONFIG_TMC5160_RUN_MA , CONFIG_TMC5160_HOLD_MA 0 (from MakeConfig() ) current CONFIG_TMC5160_MRES 0 (256 microsteps) chopper.mres CONFIG_TMC5160_STEALTHCHOP n stealth.enable CONFIG_TMC5160_UART_BAUD , CONFIG_TMC5160_UART_NODE 115200, 0 uart CONFIG_TMC5160_SPI_CHAIN_LENGTH , CONFIG_TMC5160_SPI_CHAIN_INDEX 1, 0 spi CONFIG_TMC5160_VERIFY_STARTUP n verify Without Kconfig (plain CMake, other platforms) KconfigDefaults() returns Config{} , which Validate() rejects: declare the motor yourself. Both cases are host tests. Next: Porting .

docs.text: Validate(config) checks a configuration without touching the chip, and EnsureInitialized() calls it before any I/O. It returns InvalidArgument when a field is out of range, the motor or the sense resistor is missing, a current is above the motor's ceiling, or a combination breaks a guard. CheckedConfig runs it at build time: constexpr CheckedConfig kBoard{MakeConfig(...)} does not compile when the configuration is invalid.

docs.text: Contract ¶ What the TMC5160 driver promises, what it needs, and the rules a caller follows. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Power-up reset: 25 Power-Up Reset, p. 119 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver inherits the Kokeb Labs driver contract ; this page states only what is specific to it. A change to anything here is a breaking change, listed under Breaking in the changelog . Promises ¶ The constructor is noexcept , stores the configuration, does no I/O and cannot fail. EnsureInitialized() is the only way to start the driver (there is no Begin() ). Its first call validates the stored configuration ( InvalidArgument , nothing sent), brings the bus up, quiesces the chip (TOFF 0, DRV_ENN inactive), reads IOIN and checks the version byte 0x30 ( DeviceIdMismatch ) and the strap ( ModeMismatch ), clears GSTAT and then writes every register from the configuration. On any failure the driver stays uninitialised with the power stage off and the next call starts again from the beginning; once it has succeeded, later calls return Ok with no I/O. Every call that touches the chip returns Error::NotInitialized before EnsureInitialized() succeeds. No call initialises or resets the chip as a side effect. The current never exceeds the declared motor. Every current register is derived from the declared motor and sense resistor; a request above the ceiling returns LimitExceeded and sends nothing. A bus failure between two writes never leaves a current above the ceiling. Every dangerous write is guarded. A guarded call returns an error and writes nothing; an Ack in the configuration lifts exactly one guard ( Guards ). A reset is never driven into a motor. After a chip reset the write-only registers are at their reset values; the driver returns UnexpectedReset , becomes uninitialised, and Enable() refuses (reading GSTAT first) until EnsureInitialized() has rewritten everything. The way out is never closed: Disable() , Stop() of every kind, Hold() and Deinitialize() still send their writes after a reset report. One guard serves every write that can switch the bridge on: Enable() and any chopper write while the driver is enabled ( SetChopper() , SetCurrent() , SetStandstill() and the other setters that carry CHOPCONF) read GSTAT first and, on UART, check that the interface counter equals the number of writes the driver sent. ClearFaults() and ClearGlobalStatus() read GSTAT before they clear it, so a clear never hides a reset; Deinitialize() switches the bridge off and reports a reset it finds. A UART write can be lost without a reply. The chip answers no write, so a datagram that arrives damaged is dropped silently. The driver sends each write once and learns of a loss only from the interface counter: a switching off write ( Disable() , Stop(Emergency) , the first write of start-up, ClearFaults() ) is always followed by an IFCNT read and returns VerifyFailed when the counter missed it, whatever Verify the caller passed (one extra transfer); every other UART write is unconfirmed unless the caller asks for Verify::Counter or ReadBack . A mismatch is reported, never resynchronised: the driver does not adopt the chip's counter, so a lost write cannot be hidden by the next check. A stalled axis stays stopped. With stop_on_stall the chip holds the stop until RAMP_STAT.event_stop_sg is cleared. Service() and ClearRampEvents() never clear that bit ( ClearRampEvents() returns Refused for a mask that contains it); only ReleaseStall() does, after it has written Hold, so the axis does not restart towards the old target. SetStopOnStall(false) and SetSwitches() do not release it either: with the event latched they end the ramp at the present position before SW_MODE is written. InvalidArgument means nothing was sent. Arguments are validated before the first transfer, including the node address of ProgramNode() (254 needs multi_node ), the table of SetMicrostepTable() and the sum of MoveBy() ; a MoveBy() whose target overflows is LimitExceeded after one read. A start-up ends a running ramp. In the motion-controller mode EnsureInitialized() reads RAMP_STAT and writes position mode with XTARGET = XACTUAL before it rewrites the ramp registers and SW_MODE, so a chip that stayed powered while the MCU restarted ramps down instead of turning on. It may still be decelerating: it stops past the captured XTARGET, waits TZEROWAIT and runs back to it (page 83 c). Enable() returns Busy until one RAMP_STAT read shows vzero set, t_zerowait_active clear and, in position mode with VMAX not 0, position_reached set (page 44): vzero alone is also set at the instant the ramp turns back (TZEROWAIT 0, or the end of a pause with VSTART 0). XTARGET is written before position mode, so the chip never heads for the target of the last session. A stall stop of the last session is neither released nor hidden ( BeginReport::stall_latched ). On SPI, Enable() also reads IOIN and checks VERSION (a stuck line reads zeros). A switch-off ends the ramp too. Disable() , Stop(Emergency) , ClearFaults() and Deinitialize() write VSTART 0, VMAX 0 and velocity mode after DRV_ENN and TOFF 0, and Enable() returns Busy while RAMP_STAT.vzero is clear, a TZEROWAIT pause runs or a position move with a speed has not reached its target, so a bridge that is switched on again never resumes an old move. SetHomePosition() , SetStealthChop() , EnterDirectMode() and ReleaseStall() use the same check. A position move that a switch or a stall stop holds short of its target is Busy until Stop() of any kind or Hold() ends it (velocity or hold mode, or XTARGET = XACTUAL), so a homing loop that polls SetHomePosition() after a position move never waits forever once it stops the move. A Stop() that returns Ok leaves the ramp generator commanded to stop (velocity mode with VMAX 0, or position mode with XTARGET = XACTUAL for HoldTarget ), also when the direct-mode state is in doubt (after a failed GCONF write or a failed start-up): XTARGET is then written 0 by the last write (VMAX 0 and velocity mode go first, so a chip in position mode is not sent to 0). Hold() keeps the speed. A reset report in the middle of a stop or switch-off sequence is returned only after its last write. A move starts in its own direction. MoveTo() writes XTARGET, then position mode, then VSTART and VMAX: after a stop the chip is in velocity mode with VMAX 0, where XTARGET is ignored, and position mode with VMAX 0 does not move, so the motor never runs in the old velocity direction or towards an older target first. Stop(HoldTarget) likewise writes XTARGET = XACTUAL before position mode; it decelerates past that position and, after TZEROWAIT, runs back to it (page 83 c). RunVelocity() writes the mode first from the other velocity mode and from position mode (no read there), VMAX first in the same velocity mode, and from hold mode reads VACTUAL (VMAX first at rest or running the asked way). A position ramp in its TZEROWAIT pause or turning back can start its run-back before the mode write arrives: at most VSTART t + a t^2/2 + (VSTART + a t)^2/(2 AMAX) microsteps, t the time to the accepted mode write (one 8-byte UART frame is 8.3 ms at 9600 baud), a = max(A1, AMAX) when V1 > 0 and VSTART < V1, else AMAX (page 40). TZEROWAIT longer than t avoids it (page 83 c). From position mode the old VMAX also applies for that one write. The bound counts from the call; a run-back that already moves before the call keeps its speed for that write as well, and t is at least one frame time (the port and the line add to it). VMAX stays at or above VSTART. SetMaxVelocity() refuses 0 < VMAX < VSTART (the chip's or the profile's, which the next move writes again) with InvalidArgument (page 40) and writes VSTART 0 before VMAX 0 (page 84). VMAX 0 is kept for later moves: MoveTo() and MoveBy() return Refused until SetMaxVelocity() or SetRamp() sets a speed, so a caller waiting for an arrival never waits on a move that cannot start. SPI writes are not verified unless asked. SPI has no integrity check on the wire and Config::verify is None by default: a corrupted write at start-up is not seen before Enable() . Enable() therefore sends GLOBALSCALER and IHOLD_IRUN again with Verify::Echo before it switches the bridge on (the two that set the coil current). Ask for Verify::Echo (or ReadBack ) on the calls where it matters, or set Config::verify ; the current registers cannot be read back (write-only), so Echo is the check. Direct mode starts from zero. EnterDirectMode() writes XTARGET = 0 before it sets the direct-mode bit, so a stale target cannot drive the coils. A direct-mode write that failed leaves the mode in doubt: motion calls are Refused and Stop() and Hold() write XTARGET = 0 until a later enter or exit succeeds. Stop() and Hold() in direct mode de-energise the coils (XTARGET = 0) instead of writing XACTUAL there. A line stuck at one level is reported. ReadInputs() and Service() return Bus for a reply the chip cannot produce (an SPI reply of all zeros, an IOIN whose VERSION is not 0x30 is DeviceIdMismatch ). Verify semantics. A call sends only the traffic the datasheet needs. A check that costs more traffic is asked for per call with a trailing Verify argument: None , Echo , ReadBack , Counter . A failed check returns VerifyFailed . Reading a write-only register returns Refused ; the shadow is the answer. Writes are not retried (a UART write is lost silently, see above); UART reads are retried twice. Every port failure propagates as Error::Bus or Timeout ; no getter returns a stale or zero value after a failed read. Every wait is bounded (counts of DelayUs() ). A missing DelayUs() is a compile error; a missing GpioSet() makes Enable() write TOFF only; a missing Log() logs nothing. A misdeclared hook is a compile error. Deinitialize() quiesces the chip once a start-up has begun, even after a reset report, and stays owed (the next Disable() still reaches the chip) if its write failed. A driver that never started sends nothing. Depends on ¶ Dependency Version Why A C++20 compiler GCC 10, Clang 13 or later Concepts constrain the port CMake 3.16 or later Generates tmc5160_version.h Your port The bus, within the bus requirements; the delay; optionally DRV_ENN at its idle level before the first transfer, DIAG pins, the SPI clock and logging ( Porting ) Nothing else: no RTOS, no SDK, no other repository of the org. Threading ¶ The driver is not thread-safe and takes no lock. Use each driver object from one task at a time, or guard every call on it with one mutex; the layer that owns the driver owns that lock, and the bus lock when several chips share a bus. Nothing may run in an ISR: every call can block for a bus transfer or a delay. Separate objects share no state. Errors ¶ tmc5160::Error inside tmc5160::Result<T> . Values 0 to 9 are the shared base set; this driver returns every one of them, plus five chip-specific values. Error Value Returned when Ok 0 The call succeeded NotInitialized 1 EnsureInitialized() has not succeeded, or Deinitialize() ran since InvalidArgument 2 A Config field or argument is out of range ( Validate() ); nothing was sent Bus 3 A port hook returned false Timeout 4 The chip did not answer (UART) or a bounded wait ran out DeviceIdMismatch 5 IOIN.VERSION is not 0x30 : another chip, no chip or a wiring fault Crc 6 The CRC-8 of a UART reply does not match (never produced on SPI) Busy 7 The motor is moving: the call needs standstill DeviceFault 8 The driver reports an error (GSTAT.drv_err): a short or an overtemperature Unsupported 9 The hook, bus or mode the call needs is absent UnexpectedReset 16 The chip reset: every write-only register is lost VerifyFailed 17 A write-back, echo or interface-counter check did not match Refused 18 A guard refused the call: a missing acknowledgement or an unsafe order ModeMismatch 19 The SD_MODE strap or the bus does not match Config::mode LimitExceeded 20 The request exceeds a declared motor, board or ramp limit The API guide says what to do about each. Known limits ¶ SPI has no integrity check on the wire. A corrupted reply looks like data; Enable() reads GSTAT to catch a reset since start-up, but a corrupted GSTAT reply can hide the flag. Call Service() periodically. A MISO line stuck low is noticed by Service() , the status, snapshot and standstill reads and Enable() : an all-zero reply with an all-zero status byte is checked with one IOIN read, and only a wrong VERSION is Bus (a live chip can have no flag set for a moment); a read of one other register can still return zeros that look like data. With Config::uart.multi_node , node 254 is allowed because the addressing procedure of the datasheet programs it. The chip's automatic tuning of StealthChop is waited for with the time of the A version; a chip with a longer autotune leaves the tuning unfinished (A37). Memory ¶ No heap, no exceptions, no RTTI, no std::function , no std::string , no printf and no static mutable state. A driver object holds a reference to the port, a Config (288 bytes), the shadow registers and the transfer buffers (two SPI frames of 40 bytes for a chain of 8 chips and two UART frames of 8 bytes, members of the object, never on the stack, so a port with DMA can reach them): about 960 bytes on a 64-bit host. Platform ¶ Platform-free: the same code runs on any target with a C++20 compiler, including the host tests. The ESP-IDF port in examples/esp32 is an example, not part of the driver. Deviations from the standard ¶ None.

docs.text: Coverage map ¶ Every register, bit field, mode, pin, rating and coded range of the datasheet, and where the driver handles it. The rows come from the design matrix this driver was built to: 593 rows, each with the datasheet section and printed page, the driver API that handles it and a status: Status Meaning OK The driver handles it and a host test covers it against the chip model GUARD A dangerous value or sequence: the driver refuses it unless the call carries an acknowledgement ( Guards ) INFO Documented only: a pin or rating with no driver function, a fact the application must respect TODO Out of scope by the owner's decision (OTP programming); the driver never writes it The tests are in tests/ and are named after the feature they check; nothing here has run on a chip. An OK row is backed by an assertion that fails when the handled behaviour changes (checked by the mutation run in Testing ); the DcStep (DCCTRL), encoder (ENCMODE) and bridge (DRV_CONF) bit positions are asserted field by field in tests/test_mutants.cpp . docs.text: Every register, bit field, mode, pin, rating and coded range of the datasheet, and where the driver handles it. The rows come from the design matrix this driver was built to: 593 rows, each with the datasheet section and printed page, the driver API that handles it and a status: Status Meaning OK The driver handles it and a host test covers it against the chip model GUARD A dangerous value or sequence: the driver refuses it unless the call carries an acknowledgement ( Guards ) INFO Documented only: a pin or rating with no driver function, a fact the application must respect TODO Out of scope by the owner's decision (OTP programming); the driver never writes it The tests are in tests/ and are named after the feature they check; nothing here has run on a chip. An OK row is backed by an assertion that fails when the handled behaviour changes (checked by the mutation run in Testing ); the DcStep (DCCTRL), encoder (ENCMODE) and bridge (DRV_CONF) bit positions are asserted field by field in tests/test_mutants.cpp .

docs.text: Current and limits ¶ How the motor current is derived from what you declare, and the limits the driver enforces on it. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Standstill current and power-down: 6.1 General Configuration Registers, p. 36 Selecting sense resistors and the current scale: 9 Selecting Sense Resistors, p. 74 DC and timing characteristics: 28.2 DC and Timing Characteristics, p. 121 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The formula ¶ The chip's coil RMS current is (datasheet section 9, page 74): I_rms = (GLOBALSCALER / 256) * ((CS + 1) / 32) * (VFS / Rsense) / sqrt(2) VFS is 325 mV typical with a tolerance of 5 percent (section 28.2, page 121); GLOBALSCALER 0 means 256, and values 1 to 31 are not allowed. CS is IRUN while moving and IHOLD at standstill; CoolStep lowers it between the two. What you declare ¶ You declare Field Why The motor's rated RMS current Motor::rated_rms_ma The ceiling for run and hold current A hard ceiling, if lower than rated Motor::max_rms_ma 0 means the rated current The coil resistance Motor::coil_resistance_mohm The StealthChop lower limit; 0 means unknown The sense resistor per coil Board::rsense_mohm The divisor in the formula The motor supply Board::supply_mv , supply_max_mv Checked against 10 V to 55 V; the short-protection level depends on it The ceiling ¶ units::PlanCurrent() turns a request in mA into registers. The ceiling is the smaller of max_rms_ma and rated_rms_ma , reduced by 5 percent ( Config::include_tolerance , default on) so that a chip whose full-scale voltage is 5 percent high still stays below the rated current. A request above the ceiling returns LimitExceeded and sends nothing. A request below one CS step at the smallest allowed GLOBALSCALER (129) also returns LimitExceeded : it cannot be realised; use a larger sense resistor. GLOBALSCALER is chosen in the range 129 to 256 so that the CS field has the most resolution. IHOLD above IRUN is refused unless Ack::HoldAboveRun is in Config::ack ( Guards ). The order of writes ¶ SetCurrent() changes GLOBALSCALER and IHOLD_IRUN with two writes. The driver picks the order by the intermediate current: when the new scaler is not larger than the old one (by the product with the CS value) it writes the scaler first, otherwise IHOLD_IRUN first, so a bus failure between the two writes never leaves a current above the ceiling. What the plan returns ¶ CurrentPlan holds global_scaler , irun , ihold , and the realised run_ma and hold_ma . The realised values are at or below the request, never above it. GetCurrentPlan() returns the plan in force. After a reset ¶ A chip reset sets every register to its reset value, including GLOBALSCALER 0 (256) and IRUN 0. The driver's shadow keeps the values it wrote; Enable() refuses after a reset flag so the reset values are never driven into a motor. EnsureInitialized() again rewrites everything from the configuration. The sense resistor table ¶ The datasheet's table on page 74 rounds the full-scale current up by 2 to 5 percent against the formula ( Ambiguities , A20); the driver uses the formula. Any sense resistor is accepted if the request fits: the advice outside the table's range (0.05 to 0.22 ohm) is the application's (A47).

docs.text: DIAG and status ¶ The status registers, the DIAG pins and the one call that reads the events. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Global status and interface counter: 6.1 General Configuration Registers, p. 33 Ramp status and events: 6.3 Ramp Generator Registers, p. 44 Driver status: 6.5 Motor Driver Registers, p. 55 Temperature sensors and short protection: 11 Diagnostics and Protection, p. 78 Open load diagnostics: 11.3 Open Load Diagnostics, p. 80 DIAG outputs: 16 DIAG Outputs, p. 97 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Status ¶ Call Register Content ReadGlobalStatus() GSTAT reset , drv_err , uv_cp ReadDriverStatus() DRV_STATUS StallGuard result, CS_ACTUAL, short, overtemperature, open load, standstill ReadRampStatus() RAMP_STAT Stop events, position reached, velocity reached, latch ready ReadEncoderStatus() ENC_STATUS N event, deviation warning ReadInputs() IOIN Pin levels and the version byte ReadSnapshot() several GSTAT, DRV_STATUS, RAMP_STAT, XACTUAL, VACTUAL, TSTEP, MSCNT in one batch Service() several The event registers, decoded; the latched events are cleared The write-to-clear bits of RAMP_STAT are bits 12, 7, 6, 3 and 2 (mask 0x10CC ); the read-only status bits are never written (A24). The SPI status byte ¶ Every SPI reply starts with the status byte of the previous transfer (A3). The driver reads bit 0 (reset) and bit 1 (driver error) on every call: a reset flag while the driver believes the chip is configured returns UnexpectedReset and makes the driver uninitialised; a driver error makes the motion calls return DeviceFault until ClearFaults() . Bits 7 to 2 are exposed to the application and never gate a call. DIAG0 and DIAG1 ¶ SetDiag() chooses what the pins report. In motion controller mode DIAG0 can output the internal STEP and DIAG1 the DIR; in STEP/DIR mode they report the error, the pre-warning, the stall, the index and the chopper on-state, and DIAG1 the skipped DcStep steps. Open-drain or push-pull is a bit per pin. The pins need a pull-up of 47 kOhm or less in open drain (section 16, page 97). With a GpioGet() hook, Diag0Active() and Diag1Active() read the pin level, taking the polarity into account. // A periodic service call: one batch read, the events decoded and the latched ones cleared. tmc5160 :: Error ServiceLoop ( Motor & motor ) { const auto events = motor . Service (); if ( ! events ) { return events . error ; // UnexpectedReset: write-only registers are lost, Enable() refuses } if ( events . value . driver . over_temp || events . value . driver . s2g_a || events . value . driver . s2g_b ) { return tmc5160 :: Error :: DeviceFault ; } return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; } Errors ¶ A short to ground or supply, or an overtemperature, shuts the bridge down and sets GSTAT.drv_err: the driver stays off until it is disabled and enabled again. ClearFaults() disables the driver (and stops the ramp generator), clears GSTAT and enables it again when the cause is gone and the motor stands still (a motor that still turns leaves the driver disabled and the call returns Busy : call Enable() later); while the overtemperature flag still reads set it refuses. Open load flags are informative only and are not reliable at standstill or in StealthChop (section 11.3, page 80).

docs.text: Guards and acknowledgements ¶ Which writes the driver refuses, why, and the acknowledgement that lifts a guard for one configuration. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Sample circuits and gate drive: 3 Sample Circuits, p. 15 Selecting sense resistors and the current scale: 9 Selecting Sense Resistors, p. 74 Temperature sensors and short protection: 11 Diagnostics and Protection, p. 78 DC motor and direct mode: 21 DC Motor or Solenoid, p. 110 Absolute maximum ratings and operational range: 28.1 Operational Range, p. 120 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . A stepper driver has registers that can destroy the motor or the bridge. The driver never exposes them raw: the current comes from the declared motor and sense resistor ( Current and limits ), and every other dangerous value has a guard. A guarded call returns an error and writes nothing. Acknowledgements ¶ Config::ack is a set of Ack values. Each one lifts exactly one guard, and the configuration that carries it says in code that the application accepted the risk. Ack Lifts Datasheet HoldAboveRun IHOLD above IRUN section 6.2, page 38 ShortProtectionOff diss2g or diss2vs (short protection disabled) section 11.2, page 78 LowOtLevel The 120 degree shutdown level, or 136 degrees with a supply above 24 V section 6.1, page 36 HardStopWithStealthChop A hard stop while StealthChop is enabled section 6.3, page 43 VstartAboveVstop VSTART above VSTOP section 6.3, page 41 DirectMode Direct mode (coil currents from XTARGET) section 21, page 110 VoltageModeNoCurrentLimit Direct mode with a voltage-mode chopper, which has no current limit section 21, page 110 // A guarded write: IHOLD above IRUN is refused unless the call acknowledges it. tmc5160 :: Error HoldAboveRun ( Motor & motor ) { tmc5160 :: Config c = motor . GetConfig (); c . current . hold_ma = c . current . run_ma + 100 ; const auto refused = motor . SetCurrent ( c . current . run_ma , c . current . hold_ma ); return refused . error ; // Refused: no tmc5160::Ack::HoldAboveRun in the configuration } The guards ¶ Guard Rule Result Current ceiling Run and hold current, rounded down, at most the smaller of max_rms_ma and rated_rms_ma , reduced by the 5 percent tolerance LimitExceeded Sense resistor bound The sense resistor must allow the request ( VFS / Rsense / sqrt(2) ) LimitExceeded No raw current registers GLOBALSCALER, IHOLD and IRUN are set only from a current plan; GLOBALSCALER 129 to 256 by type Hold current Hold at most run Refused Supply supply_mv 10 000 to 55 000 InvalidArgument Bridge Written only when declared; break-before-make at least 130 percent of the declared MOSFET switching time; bbm_time at most 24; only with the driver off LimitExceeded Short levels s2vs_level 4 to 15, s2g_level 2 to 15, and 12 to 15 when the highest supply is above 52 V Refused Short protection off diss2g , diss2vs Refused Overtemperature 136 C above 24 V and 120 C Refused Chopper toff 1 to 15 (0 only through Disable() ); toff 1 needs tbl 2 or more; effective hysteresis sum at most 16 InvalidArgument Thresholds TPWMTHRS at least TCOOLTHRS at least THIGH where non-zero; CoolStep and stop on stall need TCOOLTHRS InvalidArgument StealthChop With autoscale: IRUN at least 8, TPOWERDOWN at least 2, the run current above the lower limit when the coil resistance is known; only at standstill (the check of Enable() ) Refused , Busy StealthChop and stop A hard stop with StealthChop enabled Refused Soft stop and stall soft_stop together with stop_on_stall Refused DcStep Needs the default table, high_fullstep and high_const_off , TOFF 3 or more, VDCMIN 0 or 256 or more InvalidArgument Ramp VMAX within the register limit and max_velocity_reg ; D1 and VSTOP at least 1; VSTOP at least VSTART LimitExceeded , InvalidArgument Motion MoveTo() and MoveBy() need the nine ramp registers written and a VMAX that is not 0 (after SetMaxVelocity(0) , until SetMaxVelocity() or SetRamp() gives a speed again); SetMaxVelocity() refuses 0 < VMAX < VSTART (the chip's or the profile's) Refused , InvalidArgument Home position SetHomePosition() needs standstill: vzero, no TZEROWAIT pause and, in position mode with VMAX not 0, the target reached ( Stop() or Hold() ends a move a switch or stall holds) Busy Stall release ReleaseStall() holds, verifies standstill, then clears the event; the motor never restarts by itself. Switching the stop off while its event is latched first ends the ramp at the present position Busy Microstep table Only when MSCNT is 0; the decoded wave inside the allowed range; segments in order Refused Direct mode Ack::DirectMode ; entry refused while moving; currents within the range of the chopper mode Refused DIAG Bits that belong to the other mode are refused; steps_skipped is exclusive InvalidArgument UART addressing send_delay at least 2 with several nodes; node 0 to 253 (254 with multi_node ); ProgramNode() over SPI Refused , Unsupported Clock External clock 4 to 18 MHz; the SPI clock when the port reports it InvalidArgument Encoder Encoder calls in STEP/DIR mode Unsupported Registers the driver never writes ¶ OTP_PROG and FACTORY_CONF are never written (the owner excluded OTP programming; a test sends every call and checks the register was not touched). GCONF.test_mode is never set. Read-only registers are never written, and reserved bits are written as 0. After a reset ¶ Reading a write-only register returns Refused : the chip's answer is undefined (A4). The driver keeps a write-through shadow of those registers and never reads them back. A chip reset (undervoltage, power-up) clears them all: UnexpectedReset is returned, the driver becomes uninitialised, and Enable() refuses until EnsureInitialized() has rewritten everything.

docs.text: Hardware ¶ The TMC5160A's package, pins, bus settings, timing and power, as the driver uses them. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Package, pins and signal descriptions: 2 Pin Assignments, p. 11 Sample circuits and gate drive: 3 Sample Circuits, p. 15 Absolute maximum ratings and operational range: 28.1 Operational Range, p. 120 DC and timing characteristics: 28.2 DC and Timing Characteristics, p. 121 Thermal characteristics: 28.3 Thermal Characteristics, p. 124 Package mechanical data and codes: 30 Package Mechanical Data, p. 128 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver drives only DRV_ENN of the control pins. CtrlPin::DcEnable and CtrlPin::DcIn exist for a port that wires them, InputPin::DcOut likewise: no call of the driver sets or reads them. Package and pins ¶ The TMC5160 and TMC5160A are sold in a 48-pin TQFP with exposed pad (7 x 7 mm, 0.5 mm pitch) and in a wettable-flank QFN (8 x 8 mm). The driver uses the same registers on both. Each pad is coloured by the pin's electrical type (legend below). Next to it is the pin's name and, in mono, the hook of the driver's port that drives or reads it; a pin without a hook is not used by the driver. The dashed square is the exposed pad. Operating modes and straps ¶ Mode SD_MODE SPI_MODE Interface Driver Motion controller low high (SPI) or low (UART) SPI or UART Mode::MotionController STEP/DIR with serial configuration high high SPI Mode::StepDir Standalone STEP/DIR, configured by the CFG pins high low none not drivable EnsureInitialized() reads IOIN and compares the SD_MODE level with Config::mode ; a mismatch returns ModeMismatch . Control pins ¶ The driver drives DRV_ENN, and no other control pin, through the optional GpioSet() hook, with logical levels: GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "driver enabled", which your port writes as a low level on DRV_ENN. A board that wires DRV_ENN low permanently leaves the hook out: Enable() then writes TOFF only, and Disable() writes TOFF 0. Configure the pin with the driver off before it becomes an output. DIAG0 and DIAG1 are read with GpioGet() . They are open drain by default and need a pull-up of 47 kOhm or less. docs.text: The driver drives DRV_ENN, and no other control pin, through the optional GpioSet() hook, with logical levels: GpioSignal::ACTIVE means "driver enabled", which your port writes as a low level on DRV_ENN. A board that wires DRV_ENN low permanently leaves the hook out: Enable() then writes TOFF only, and Disable() writes TOFF 0. Configure the pin with the driver off before it becomes an output. DIAG0 and DIAG1 are read with GpioGet() . They are open drain by default and need a pull-up of 47 kOhm or less.

docs.text: Installation ¶ Add the driver to a CMake project on any MCU or on your PC, or to an ESP-IDF project. It is a header-only C++20 library with no dependencies, and one root CMakeLists.txt serves every build. Requirements ¶ A C++20 compiler: GCC 10+, Clang 13+ or a current MSVC. The driver uses concepts and requires . CMake 3.16 or later: it generates the version header the driver includes ( tmc5160_version.h ). No RTOS, heap, exceptions or RTTI: every call is noexcept and returns a Result . Get the source ¶ A git submodule keeps the driver pinned to the version you chose: git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc5160.git external/driver-tmc5160 git submodule update --init external/driver-tmc5160 Only inc/ , src/ , cmake/ , _config/ and CMakeLists.txt are needed to build. The examples are not; the ESP32 example even has its own submodule ( examples/esp32/scripts ). CMake (any MCU, any host) ¶ This is the MCU-neutral path: the same two lines work for a host build, STM32 (CubeMX CMake projects), RP2040 (Pico SDK), nRF (nRF Connect SDK) or any other CMake toolchain. Platforms lists what has a port today. add_subdirectory ( external/driver-tmc5160 ) target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tmc5160::tmc5160 ) tmc5160::tmc5160 is an alias of the tmc5160 INTERFACE target. It carries the include directories (the headers and the generated version header) and requires C++20, so your target does not need to set either. Option Default Effect TMC5160_ENABLE_WARNINGS OFF -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic on every target that links the driver TMC5160_BUILD_TESTS OFF Builds the host tests in tests/ and the host example ( Testing and CI ) Installed package ¶ To use the driver without adding its source tree to your build, install it and find the package: cmake -S external/driver-tmc5160 -B build-tmc5160 cmake --install build-tmc5160 --prefix /opt/sdk find_package ( tmc5160 0.1 REQUIRED ) # with CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=/opt/sdk target_link_libraries ( my_app PRIVATE tmc5160::tmc5160 ) The target is tmc5160::tmc5160 in both cases ( EXPORT_NAME ), so a project can switch between add_subdirectory() and find_package() without changing its target_link_libraries() . The headers and the generated tmc5160_version.h go to include/tmc5160/inc/ , the template implementation to include/tmc5160/src/tmc5160.ipp . The host CI installs the package and builds a consumer against it on every pull request ( Testing and CI ). ESP-IDF ¶ Under ESP-IDF the root CMakeLists.txt registers the repository itself as a component: with ESP_PLATFORM set it calls idf_component_register() from the same build settings, with the menu in _config/Kconfig . There is no wrapper to copy. ESP-IDF names a component after its folder, so the name in your REQUIRES is the name of the folder the repository is in. Pick one of these: How What to write Component name Folder of extra components list(APPEND EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS external/driver-tmc5160) in the project CMakeLists.txt , before project.cmake driver-tmc5160 (the folder) Submodule under components/ git submodule add https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc5160.git components/tmc5160 tmc5160 (the folder) Component manager, from git The dependency below in main/idf_component.yml tmc5160 (the key) # main/idf_component.yml of your project dependencies : tmc5160 : git : https://github.com/kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-tmc5160.git version : v0.1.0 # a release tag Your component then declares REQUIRES tmc5160 (or the folder name), and idf.py menuconfig shows the driver's menu ( Configuration ). The ESP32 example uses the first way, with EXTRA_COMPONENT_DIRS pointing at the repository root, and works out the folder name in main/CMakeLists.txt ; CI builds it on every pull request. The repository has no idf_component.yml . The component manager does not need one for a git dependency; the manifest is only required to publish to the ESP Component Registry, which these releases do not use. If registry publishing is chosen, the manifest is added at the root then. How the build is organised ¶ Layer File Role Settings cmake/tmc5160_build_settings.cmake Target name, include directories, sources, version: the single source of truth Library CMakeLists.txt INTERFACE target, alias, install rules and the package export, or the ESP-IDF component Tool configuration _config/ Doxyfile, the docs site, Kconfig, clang-format, clang-tidy and the linters Version ¶ The version is set once in the settings file and written into tmc5160_version.h in the build tree at configure time. The Doxyfile ( _config/Doxyfile ) carries a copy; a host test fails when it differs. Read it at run time: const char * v = tmc5160 :: GetDriverVersion (); // "0.1.0" Next ¶ Quickstart runs the driver on your PC, then on your MCU; Porting writes the port for your MCU.

docs.text: Mechanization policy ¶ Where each defect class of the catalogue is caught, and how a class moves to a cheaper catch. The goal: a defect is found by the cheapest check that can find it, and reviewers spend their time on judgement, not on what a script can do. Decision rule ¶ Catch a class at the first level that can decide it without judgement, in order of cost: Lint ( tools/preflight.sh , runs in seconds, on every builder's machine). Use it when the defect is a pattern in text or syntax: a forbidden include, a MISRA rule CodeQL reports, a missing else , a parameter name, a symbol named in docs that does not exist, a missing gitlink. Test, model or mutation (host tests, the chip model's fault knobs, fuzz properties, compile-fail cases, mutants of a fix). Use it when the defect is behaviour: what the driver sends or returns when the chip or the bus misbehaves. A test is the right level when the model can be made to misbehave in exactly that way. Independent review question (a reviewer who did not write the code). Use it only for what needs judgement: whether the datasheet was read correctly, whether a state machine is complete, whether the model is independent of the driver, whether a doc claim is true. Every catalogue entry names its level under DETECTION. A class with no lint or test is a review class and costs reviewer time every round; it is a candidate for promotion. Promotion ¶ A defect that reached a reviewer or the CI of a second driver is promoted one level up: review to test, test to lint where a pattern exists. The reviewer who finds the second occurrence writes the promotion item in the round's report; the template maintainer (the agent or person that owns the template branch) implements it before the next driver's first push, or records why it cannot be mechanised in the catalogue entry. A defect that reached a third driver after its promotion means the check is wrong: fix the check first, then look at the driver. Demotion never happens by silence: a check is removed only with a catalogue note saying what replaced it. What a lint may and may not do ¶ It reports file:line , the catalogue id, and the fix. It exits non-zero on a finding, in the preflight and the gate. It has no false-positive tolerance : before merging, it runs over every finished driver and the template; any finding on a driver that CI shows clean is a false positive, and the lint is not merged until it has none (narrow the pattern; do not add an ignore list per driver). It may be conservative the other way (miss cases): then the catalogue says partial and names the review question that covers the rest. It never edits files, never skips silently (a missing tool is reported as a skipped step in the final line, and the gate treats a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step as a failure), and has a selftest with one bad and one good case. It does not replace the CI scan: CI is the final word for MISRA. Recording a new finding ¶ Append the finding to its catalogue entry (driver, review round or CI report file, finding id) and update the count and the index table; add a new entry only when no class fits. Write the check at the level the rules above give: the lint, or the test pattern (model knob, mutant, fuzz property), or the reviewer's question in the skill. Run it over the finished drivers (lint) or add the regression test that fails without the fix (test). Add a CHANGELOG.md entry under [Unreleased] and the template change is released as a new template commit; drivers take it with scaffold.py --check-drift --fix (the skills and tools are managed files), which updates the template pin in .kokeb/template.yml . Mention the catalogue id in the commit subject. The pre-push gate ¶ A driver is cleared for its first push only by kokeb-tools/gate.sh <chip> (the orchestrator's script, one run per driver through the shared Docker lock). It writes a log and a verdict, and PASS needs all of: container preflight ( tools/preflight.sh --container ) with 0 failure(s) and 0 gate failure(s) , including the MISRA scan and the ESP32 builds; a skipped MISRA or ESP32 step is a FAIL; handbook_check reports 0 errors (this includes the library-subset include scan); tools/check_standalone.py passes; template drift: scaffold.py --check-drift reports nothing; no .pdf file is tracked; the examples/esp32/scripts gitlink (mode 160000) is present; the tree is staged as it will be committed. No silent skips: every step prints a line, and a missing tool fails the gate. Roles ¶ Builders write code, models, tests and docs and run host tests and the quick preflight. They do not run the container gate, push, or create repositories. The gate runner is one serialized worker that runs gate.sh for one driver at a time and reports the verdict and the log; it does not edit the driver. Reviewers are read-only and independent. They are given the code, the model, the datasheet, the catalogue and the previous round's report, and never the builder's conclusions (the build report is read only in the claims-vs-code step). They run the review-round protocol. Fixers change the driver, fix at the cause, add the test that fails without the fix, and answer each finding id. The template maintainer applies promotions and keeps the catalogue current. Backlog of promotions (state of the catalogue) ¶ The classes whose target level is above their present level are listed in the catalogue index: RD-12 to RD-18 and RD-23 (MISRA patterns, one misra_lint with a rule per id), RD-20 and RD-22 (ESP-IDF and compile-fail lints), RD-08 ( claims-symbols ), RD-07 (model standalone lint), RD-06, RD-01, RD-02, RD-03, RD-05, RD-10 and RD-25 (shared model knobs and a template mutation runner), RD-21 (host start-up test of the ESP32 port).

docs.text: Microstep table ¶ The 256-entry sine table, how the register words are decoded and how a custom table is checked. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Sine-wave look-up table: 18 Sine-Wave Look-up Table, p. 105 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The sequencer drives the coil currents from a table of 256 entries of one quarter of a sine wave. It is stored as eight 32-bit words MSLUT0 to MSLUT7 of 1-bit increments, with the segment boundaries in MSLUTSEL and the two start values in MSLUTSTART (section 18.2, page 105). Decoding (A6) ¶ The datasheet says on page 47 that bit n is "the difference between entry x and x+1" and on page 105 that the table starts at START_SIN and steps up. Decoding the default words with the page 105 rule and comparing them with the formula on page 49, round(248 * sin(2 pi i / 1024 + pi / 1024)) - 1 , matches all 256 entries only when bit n is the increment into entry n. The driver decodes that way; the model has a switch for the literal reading, and a test shows both readings agree within one count. START_SIN90 is a separate field for entry 256. A custom table ¶ SetMicrostepTable() accepts a table only when MSCNT was just read as 0, and checks it before writing: the decoded wave must stay within -248 to 247, the segments must be ordered (X1 below X2 below X3), and START_SIN90 must be consistent. A bad table returns Refused and writes nothing. DcStep needs the default table. A table written in a previous session is not rewritten by EnsureInitialized() when MSCNT is not 0. Reading the position in the table ¶ ReadMicrostepCounter() returns MSCNT (0 to 1023); ReadMicrostepCurrents() decodes MSCURACT into the two signed 9-bit coil currents (A7). MSCNT equals XACTUAL modulo 1024 at 256 microsteps.

docs.text: Motion ¶ The ramp generator, the two motion modes, the units of the ramp registers and the calls that move and stop the motor. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Velocity dependent control: 6.2 Velocity Dependent Driver Feature Control Register Set, p. 38 Ramp generator registers: 6.3 Ramp Generator Registers, p. 40 Reference switches and SW_MODE: 6.3 Ramp Generator Registers, p. 43 Ramp status and events: 6.3 Ramp Generator Registers, p. 44 Real world unit conversion: 12.1 Real World Unit Conversion, p. 81 Motion profiles and early ramp termination: 12.2 Motion Profiles, p. 82 Velocity thresholds: 12.3 Velocity Thresholds, p. 84 Reference switches: 12.4 Reference Switches, p. 85 STEP/DIR interface and MicroPlyer: 15 STEP/DIR Interface, p. 94 Emergency stop: 19 Emergency Stop, p. 106 Clock oscillator and input: 26 Clock Oscillator and Input, p. 119 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Modes ¶ Mode Config::mode Strap Moves by Motion controller MotionController SD_MODE low The internal ramp generator: MoveTo() , MoveBy() , RunVelocity() STEP/DIR StepDir SD_MODE high Pulses on STEP and DIR; MicroPlyer interpolates to 256 microsteps EnsureInitialized() reads IOIN and compares the SD_MODE strap with Config::mode ; a mismatch returns ModeMismatch and the chip is left with the driver off. In STEP/DIR mode the ramp calls return Unsupported . The ramp profile ¶ RampProfile holds the six-point ramp of the datasheet (section 6.3, page 40): VSTART, A1, V1, AMAX, VMAX, DMAX, D1, VSTOP and TZEROWAIT. SetRamp() writes all of them before any XTARGET, so a move never starts on half a profile. The defaults are the datasheet's quick-start values. Velocities are in the chip's own unit (microsteps per 2^24 clocks); acceleration in fCLK^2 / (512 * 256 * 2^24) per second. // Position mode: the ramp generator moves to XTARGET. Poll PositionReached(). tmc5160 :: Error GoTo ( Motor & motor , int32_t target ) { if ( auto r = motor . MoveTo ( target ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } for ( int i = 0 ; i < 1000 ; ++ i ) { // bounded: the caller decides how long a move may take const auto done = motor . PositionReached (); if ( ! done ) { return done . error ; } if ( done . value ) { return tmc5160 :: Error :: Ok ; } } return tmc5160 :: Error :: Timeout ; } Units ¶ units::VelocityRegFromHz(hz, fclk) and units::AccelRegFromHzPerS() convert real-world values to register values, with a 128-bit oracle in the tests. The relations (section 12.1, page 81): v[Hz] = v_reg * fCLK / 2^24 , a[Hz/s] = a_reg * fCLK^2 / (512 * 256 * 2^24) . With the internal 12 MHz clock one velocity count is 0.715 Hz. The clock is Config::clock : an external clock changes every value. Calls ¶ Call What it does MoveTo(position) Position mode, XTARGET = position MoveBy(delta) Position mode relative to XACTUAL; a target that overflows is LimitExceeded (after one read) RunVelocity(v) Velocity mode; the sign picks the direction (write order and the run-back bound below) SetMaxVelocity(v) VMAX while moving; above Config::max_velocity_reg it returns LimitExceeded , below VSTART (not 0) InvalidArgument ; 0 writes VSTART 0 first (page 84) Hold() RAMPMODE Hold: the present velocity stays (a stop event still ends it); use Stop() to slow down Stop(kind) Ramp , Immediate , HoldTarget or Emergency (early ramp termination, section 12.2.4, page 83) SetHomePosition(x) XACTUAL and XTARGET together; needs standstill ReadPosition() , ReadVelocity() , ReadTarget() , PositionReached() The motion state Emergency switches the driver off (DRV_ENN and TOFF 0): the motor is not held, and the ramp generator is told to stop (VMAX 0, velocity mode) so that a later Enable() does not resume the move; Enable() returns Busy until RAMP_STAT shows vzero set, no TZEROWAIT pause and, in position mode with VMAX not 0, position_reached. On UART the TOFF 0 write has no reply, so Disable() and Emergency read IFCNT afterwards (one extra transfer) and return VerifyFailed when the chip did not count the write; DRV_ENN, when wired, is already high by then. Without a DRV_ENN hook a lost write leaves the chopper on, which only the error tells. Writing XACTUAL in position mode starts a move, so SetHomePosition() writes the hold mode first. Reference switches and homing ¶ SetSwitches() programs SW_MODE: stop on the left or right switch, polarity, swap, and the latches. The latched position is ReadLatchedPosition() . Homing is not a driver call: the right speed, back-off and sequence depend on the machine. examples/host/homing_switch.cpp and homing_stall.cpp show both procedures with the driver's primitives. They home in velocity mode. A position move that a switch or a stall stops has not reached its target, so SetHomePosition() answers Busy for it until Stop() (any kind) or Hold() ends the move: a homing loop that polls SetHomePosition() after a position move must stop it first, or it waits forever. After a position move arrives, the chip waits TZEROWAIT before the next move (pages 41, 83), and the standstill check answers Busy during that pause too. RunVelocity() called while a position stop pauses for TZEROWAIT or turns back after an overshoot: the ramp may start its run-back before the mode write arrives, by at most VSTART t + a t^2/2 + (VSTART + a t)^2/(2 AMAX) microsteps, t the time to the accepted mode write (one SPI datagram; one 8-byte UART frame, 80 bit times: 8.3 ms at 9600 baud, 0.7 ms at 115200) and a = max(A1, AMAX) when V1 > 0 and VSTART < V1, else AMAX (V1 = 0 disables A1, page 40). A TZEROWAIT longer than t avoids it (page 83 c). From position mode the motor also keeps, or speeds towards, the old VMAX for that one write before the new VMAX applies. The bound counts from the call: a run-back that already moves keeps its speed for that write too, and 8.3 ms is the least t at 9600 baud (the port and the line add to it). A new MoveTo() (or MoveBy() ) while a Stop(HoldTarget) pauses for TZEROWAIT retargets at once: the RAMPMODE write ends the pause (A51), and the ramp heads for the new target without the rest of the wait. SetMaxVelocity() during the pause changes only the speed of the run-back that follows. Wait for the pause to end (the standstill check is Busy until then) when the extra wait matters to the mechanics. SetMaxVelocity(0) stops a position move (VSTART 0 first, page 84) and stays in force: MoveTo() and MoveBy() return Refused until SetMaxVelocity() or SetRamp() gives a speed again. XACTUAL units ¶ In the model and on the chip, XACTUAL counts microsteps at 256 per full step; MSCNT is XACTUAL & 1023 in the sequencer. TSTEP is fCLK / |v_hz| with 256 microsteps (section 6.2, page 38). Limits ¶ Config::max_velocity_reg is an optional ceiling for VMAX beyond the register limit of 2^23 - 512 ; a ramp above it is refused. A VSTOP below 10 gives a slow termination (section 12.5, page 86): this is documented advice, not a guard.
