Without a DRV_ENN hook a lost write leaves the chopper on, which only the error tells. Writing XACTUAL in position mode starts a move, so SetHomePosition() writes the hold mode first.
docs.title: Calls

docs.text: SetSwitches() programs SW_MODE: stop on the left or right switch, polarity, swap, and the latches. The latched position is ReadLatchedPosition() . Homing is not a driver call: the right speed, back-off and sequence depend on the machine. examples/host/homing_switch.cpp and homing_stall.cpp show both procedures with the driver's primitives. They home in velocity mode. A position move that a switch or a stall stops has not reached its target, so SetHomePosition() answers Busy for it until Stop() (any kind) or Hold() ends the move: a homing loop that polls SetHomePosition() after a position move must stop it first, or it waits forever. After a position move arrives, the chip waits TZEROWAIT before the next move (pages 41, 83), and the standstill check answers Busy during that pause too. RunVelocity() called while a position stop pauses for TZEROWAIT or turns back after an overshoot: the ramp may start its run-back before the mode write arrives, by at most VSTART t + a t^2/2 + (VSTART + a t)^2/(2 AMAX) microsteps, t the time to the accepted mode write (one SPI datagram; one 8-byte UART frame, 80 bit times: 8.3 ms at 9600 baud, 0.7 ms at 115200) and a = max(A1, AMAX) when V1 > 0 and VSTART < V1, else AMAX (V1 = 0 disables A1, page 40). A TZEROWAIT longer than t avoids it (page 83 c). From position mode the motor also keeps, or speeds towards, the old VMAX for that one write before the new VMAX applies. The bound counts from the call: a run-back that already moves keeps its speed for that write too, and 8.3 ms is the least t at 9600 baud (the port and the line add to it). A new MoveTo() (or MoveBy() ) while a Stop(HoldTarget) pauses for TZEROWAIT retargets at once: the RAMPMODE write ends the pause (A51), and the ramp heads for the new target without the rest of the wait. SetMaxVelocity() during the pause changes only the speed of the run-back that follows. Wait for the pause to end (the standstill check is Busy until then) when the extra wait matters to the mechanics. SetMaxVelocity(0) stops a position move (VSTART 0 first, page 84) and stays in force: MoveTo() and MoveBy() return Refused until SetMaxVelocity() or SetRamp() gives a speed again.
docs.title: Reference switches and homing

docs.text: In the model and on the chip, XACTUAL counts microsteps at 256 per full step; MSCNT is XACTUAL & 1023 in the sequencer. TSTEP is fCLK / |v_hz| with 256 microsteps (section 6.2, page 38).
docs.title: XACTUAL units

docs.text: Config::max_velocity_reg is an optional ceiling for VMAX beyond the register limit of 2^23 - 512 ; a ramp above it is refused. A VSTOP below 10 gives a slow termination (section 12.5, page 86): this is documented advice, not a guard.
docs.title: Limits

docs.text: Porting ¶ Run the driver on a new MCU by writing one class: the SPI port or the UART port. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: SPI datagram, status byte and timing: 4 SPI Interface, p. 23 UART datagram, node address and SENDDELAY: 5.1 Datagram Structure, p. 26 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . The driver never calls your SDK. It calls hooks on a class you derive from tmc5160::SpiInterface<Self> or tmc5160::UartInterface<Self> (in inc/tmc5160_spi_interface.hpp and inc/tmc5160_uart_interface.hpp ). The base uses CRTP and declares no hook itself; the driver template is constrained by the SpiPort or UartPort concept, which checks each hook's exact signature and noexcept , so calls are resolved at compile time (no virtual functions, nothing to allocate) and a missing or misdeclared hook is a compile error at the point of use. A port is one bus or the other, never both. What you implement ¶ Method Required Contract bool EnsureInitialized() noexcept yes Bring the bus up on the first call; return true at once afterwards. false makes the driver's EnsureInitialized() return Bus bool Transfer(const uint8_t* tx, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t len) noexcept SPI One full-duplex transfer of len bytes with CSN low for all of them; len is 5 times the chain length; both buffers are given. false on any bus error BusStatus Exchange(const uint8_t* tx, std::size_t tx_len, uint8_t* rx, std::size_t rx_len, uint32_t timeout_us) noexcept UART Send tx_len bytes, then receive exactly rx_len (0 for a write). On a shared single wire read and drop the echo of your own bytes. Ok , Timeout or Fault void DelayUs(uint32_t us) noexcept yes, for every wait Wait at least us microseconds bool GpioSet(CtrlPin, GpioSignal) noexcept no Drive DRV_ENN (and the DcStep inputs); false if the pin write failed bool GpioGet(InputPin, bool& level) noexcept no Read DIAG0, DIAG1 or the DcStep output; false if the read failed uint32_t SckHz() const noexcept no The SPI clock in use, checked against the chip's limit void Log(LogLevel, const char* message) noexcept no Print one line; message is plain text, never a format string The SPI port ¶ my_port.hpp class MyPort : public tmc5160 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One transfer, CS low for all `len` bytes (5 bytes per chip in a chain). `rx` is never nullptr. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the ramp-down waits, the tuning wait and the UART recovery // depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the transfer must follow: One call, one frame. Keep CSN low for all len bytes; the chip decodes the datagram when CSN rises. For a chain, len is 5 bytes per chip. Never split a datagram into several transfers. The bus requirements below : mode 3, MSB first, up to kMaxClockHz . Start at 1 MHz on jumper wires. Raw bytes only. Do not interpret, retry or reorder bytes; the driver owns the framing and the retries. Return false for a bus error. The driver turns it into Error::Bus and never ignores it. Bounded time-outs. A stuck bus fails the call; it does not block forever. The UART port ¶ class MyUartPort : public tmc5160 :: UartInterface < MyUartPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_uart_init (); } return ready_ ; } // Send `tx_len` bytes, then receive exactly `rx_len` (0 for a write). On a shared single wire the // port reads and drops the echo of its own bytes first. Timeout: no (complete) reply within // `timeout_us`. tmc5160 :: BusStatus Exchange ( const uint8_t * tx , std :: size_t tx_len , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t rx_len , uint32_t timeout_us ) noexcept { return platform_uart_exchange ( tx , tx_len , rx , rx_len , timeout_us ); } void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; Rules the exchange must follow: Flush first. Discard bytes left over from an earlier timeout before sending. Echo. With TX and RX joined on one wire, read tx_len bytes of echo and drop them before the reply. Timeout. Wait at most timeout_us for the whole reply; return Timeout for none or a short one, Fault for a driver or hardware error. The driver adds the SENDDELAY and a margin of 64 bit times to the timeout. A write has rx_len 0. Return Ok when every byte was sent. Baud rate. Any value from 9000 up to fCLK / 16 ; declare it in Config::uart.baud . Bus requirements ¶ The driver states what the TMC5160 needs from the bus as constexpr values (handbook KB-CPP-123). Check your port's settings against them with static_assert , as both example ports do, so a port that clocks too fast or in the wrong mode does not compile: Constant Value Meaning kSpiMode 3 SCK idles high, data latched on the rising edge (section 4.3) kMsbFirst true Most significant bit first kMaxClockHz 4'000'000 f_SCK max with the internal clock kDatagramBytes 5 One datagram, 40 bits, per chip kMinCsHighNs 200 CSN high between two datagrams kCsSetupNs 10 CSN low to the first SCK edge kCsHoldNs 100 Last SCK edge to CSN high kUartDataBits 8 8N1 kUartGapResetBits 63 A longer gap between start bits resets the receiver kMaxBaudRate 750000 fCLK/16 with the internal clock kTurnaroundUs 12500 Last request byte to the first reply byte, at most Control pins ¶ Each control pin has a defined idle level, and the port drives it there before it enables the pin's output and before the driver's first transfer (handbook KB-HW-018). Configuring a pin as an output first and setting its level afterwards gives the chip a pulse it did not ask for: DRV_ENN would enable the power stage for an instant. CtrlPin Package pin Polarity Idle ( INACTIVE ) level Before the first transfer DrvEnn DRV_ENN active low high (driver off) Set high, then enable the output DcEnable ENCB_DCEN_CFG4 active high low Never driven by the driver; wire it on the board DcIn ENCA_DCIN_CFG5 active high low Never driven by the driver; wire it on the board GpioSignal::ACTIVE always means "function asserted"; the port maps it to the electrical level. A pin tied on the board needs no hook. Optional hooks ¶ The driver finds the optional hooks at compile time, in one place ( tmc5160::detail ). A missing hook falls back in a documented, safe way or fails to compile; it never skips a step silently. Hook Used for Without it DelayUs() The StealthChop tuning wait, ramp-down waits, UART recovery Compile error at the first call that waits (every port needs it in practice) GpioSet() DRV_ENN in Enable() and Disable() Enable() writes TOFF only GpioGet() Diag0Active() , Diag1Active() Those calls return Unsupported SckHz() The SPI clock check at start-up The clock is not checked Log() One line per lifecycle event or failure Nothing is logged A port with every hook: class FullPort : public tmc5160 :: SpiInterface < FullPort > { public : bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { return platform_spi_init (); } bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Required by every call that waits. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } // Optional: DRV_ENN on a GPIO. ACTIVE means "driver enabled", which is a LOW level on the pin. bool GpioSet ( tmc5160 :: CtrlPin pin , tmc5160 :: GpioSignal signal ) noexcept { if ( pin != tmc5160 :: CtrlPin :: DrvEnn ) { return false ; } return platform_gpio_write ( kDrvEnnGpio , signal == tmc5160 :: GpioSignal :: INACTIVE ); } // Optional: DIAG0 and DIAG1 as inputs. `level` is true for a high pin. bool GpioGet ( tmc5160 :: InputPin pin , bool & level ) noexcept { if ( pin == tmc5160 :: InputPin :: Diag0 ) { return platform_gpio_read ( kDiag0Gpio , level ); } return false ; } // Optional: the SPI clock in use; the driver checks the datasheet limit of the clock source. [[ nodiscard ]] uint32_t SckHz () const noexcept { return platform_spi_clock_hz (); } // Optional: one line per lifecycle event or failure. The driver never formats; the port does. void Log ( tmc5160 :: LogLevel level , const char * message ) noexcept { if ( level > tmc5160 :: LogLevel :: Warning ) { return ; } platform_log ( message ); // plain text: never use it as a format string } private : static constexpr int kDrvEnnGpio = 4 ; static constexpr int kDiag0Gpio = 5 ; }; A GpioSet() that returns void , a GpioGet() with the wrong level type and an SckHz() that is not const are compile errors: the driver must see a failed pin write. The compile-fail tests check each rule. Reference implementations ¶ Every port lives with its example, in examples/<platform>/ ; the driver has none. Platforms lists them and how to add one. examples/host/host_tmc5160_port.hpp : any PC, against a simulated chip, SPI and UART. Start from it for a host build or a test bench; it is also the smallest complete port. examples/esp32/main/esp32_tmc5160_port.hpp : ESP-IDF, SPI and UART, with every hook. Start from it for any ESP-IDF target. Check your port ¶ Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that IOIN.VERSION read 0x30 with the strap you expect. Call ReadStepTime() and ReadInterfaceCounter() (UART): they must succeed without the motor moving. Call SetCurrent() with a small current, Enable() and MoveBy(51200) with the motor loose on the bench. Threads ¶ The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract . Editor setup ¶ The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

docs.text: Build it: the ports on this page are compiled by the host CI from tests/docs/ , with the driver instantiated over them. Call EnsureInitialized() : Ok proves that writes and reads work and that IOIN.VERSION read 0x30 with the strap you expect. Call ReadStepTime() and ReadInterfaceCounter() (UART): they must succeed without the motor moving. Call SetCurrent() with a small current, Enable() and MoveBy(51200) with the motor loose on the bench.
docs.title: Check your port

docs.text: The driver is not thread-safe. Give each driver object one owner task, or guard every call with one mutex. When several chips share a bus, the port must also serialise the bus. See Contract .
docs.title: Threads

docs.text: The clang-format and clang-tidy configuration is in _config/ , and the repository root has no copy of it. Tools that take a path use it directly; CI does the same: Tool Setting Command line clang-format --style=file:_config/.clang-format , clang-tidy --config-file=_config/.clang-tidy -p build VS Code (C/C++ extension) "C_Cpp.clang_format_style": "file:${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-format" and "C_Cpp.codeAnalysis.clangTidy.args": ["--config-file=${workspaceFolder}/_config/.clang-tidy"] clangd (VS Code clangd, Neovim, Emacs), CLion These find .clang-format and .clang-tidy only by name, from the file upwards: copy both to the root once ( cp _config/.clang-format _config/.clang-tidy . ). .gitignore lists the copies, so they never reach a commit; copy again after _config/ changes Configure with -DCMAKE_EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS=ON (clangd: --compile-commands-dir=build ) so the editor sees the same flags as the build.

docs.text: Quickstart ¶ From a bare chip to a moving motor: wire it, write the port, declare the motor, move it. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Package, pins and signal descriptions: 2 Pin Assignments, p. 11 Quick configuration guide: 22 Quick Configuration Guide, p. 111 Initialization examples: 23.1 Initialization Examples, p. 116 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . 1. Wire it ¶ SPI is the default bus. The pins are in Hardware ; the minimum is SCK, MOSI, MISO, CSN, VCC_IO, ground, the motor supply and the bridge, with SPI_MODE high, SD_MODE low and CLK low for the internal 12 MHz clock. Wire DRV_ENN to a GPIO: the driver then switches the power stage in Enable() and Disable() . For UART, tie SPI_MODE and SD_MODE low and use the single wire on DIAG1_SWP ( UART protocol ). Before the first power-up: the sense resistor must be the one you declare, and the motor's rated current must be the one on its data sheet. The driver derives every current register from those two numbers. 2. Write the port ¶ The port is a class with EnsureInitialized() , Transfer() and DelayUs() . Porting has the contract. class MyPort : public tmc5160 :: SpiInterface < MyPort > { public : // Bring the bus up once; later calls return true at once. bool EnsureInitialized () noexcept { if ( ! ready_ ) { ready_ = platform_spi_init (); } return ready_ ; } // One transfer, CS low for all `len` bytes (5 bytes per chip in a chain). `rx` is never nullptr. bool Transfer ( const uint8_t * tx , uint8_t * rx , std :: size_t len ) noexcept { return platform_spi_transfer ( tx , rx , len ); } // Wait at least `us` microseconds: the ramp-down waits, the tuning wait and the UART recovery // depend on it. void DelayUs ( uint32_t us ) noexcept { platform_delay_us ( us ); } private : bool ready_ = false ; }; 3. Declare the motor and move it ¶ #include "tmc5160.hpp" int spin_one_revolution ( MyPort & port ) { // 1. Declare the motor and the board. The driver derives every current register from these two. const tmc5160 :: Config config = tmc5160 :: MakeConfig ( tmc5160 :: Motor {. rated_rms_ma = 1000 , . coil_resistance_mohm = 6000 }, tmc5160 :: Board {. rsense_mohm = 100 , . supply_mv = 24'000 }); tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > motor ( port , config ); // no I/O yet if ( auto r = motor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { // 2. bus, strap, VERSION, every register, driver off return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); // Bus, Timeout, DeviceIdMismatch, InvalidArgument ... } if ( auto r = motor . Enable (); ! r ) { // 3. DRV_ENN active, TOFF written return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } if ( auto r = motor . MoveTo ( 51'200 ); ! r ) { // 4. one revolution at 256 microsteps, 200 full steps return static_cast < int > ( r . error ); } return 0 ; // poll PositionReached(); Disable() when done } What each step does: MakeConfig() fills a Config with the datasheet's reset values, a run current of 85 percent of the motor's ceiling and a hold current of 30 percent of the run current. Config{} alone is not usable: it has no motor and no sense resistor, so Validate() rejects it. EnsureInitialized() brings the bus up, reads IOIN to check the strap and the version byte ( 0x30 ), clears the reset flag, writes every register in a safe order with the driver off, and optionally verifies the writes ( Config::verify ). On a failure it leaves the chip with the driver off. Enable() reads the global status first: after a chip reset or a driver fault it refuses ( UnexpectedReset , DeviceFault ), because the write-only registers would be at their reset values. On UART it also checks that the interface counter counted every write. MoveTo() writes XTARGET in position mode. Poll PositionReached() ; Stop() , Hold() and Disable() end the move. 4. Try it without hardware ¶ The host examples run the same calls against a simulated chip: Examples . If it does not work ¶ Troubleshooting lists each error with its usual cause. The first two to check: DeviceIdMismatch (wrong chip, wrong SPI mode, MISO stuck) and ModeMismatch (the strap does not match the bus).

docs.text: Recurring defects ¶ The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver. data 3 review test RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something 2 test test RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused 4 review test RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack 4 review test RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading 2 review lint + review RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim 3 review lint RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks 6 review review (claims check) RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard 5 review test RD-11 Header outside the library subset 2 lint lint RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic 3 CI lint RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses 2 CI lint RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain 3 CI lint RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value 1 CI lint RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ 1 CI lint RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type 4 review lint (partial) + Guards no test kills (surviving mutants) 6 review test RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules 3 review test RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI 4 CI lint RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing 6 review review RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit 3 review review RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard 3 test test RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read 2 review test RD-32 Docs style: line length, merged bullets, stale text 3 lint lint RD-33 Another project's name or dated history 1 lint lint RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check 3 lint lint Chip-protocol and safety classes ¶ RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset ¶ Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?" RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read ¶ Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?" RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data ¶ Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?" RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something ¶ Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?" RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused ¶ Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends." RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack ¶ Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?" RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading ¶ Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?" RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard ¶ Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?" RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard ¶ Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?" RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read ¶ Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b. Datasheet and documentation classes ¶ RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing ¶ Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?" RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit ¶ Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?" RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks ¶ Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return. RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim ¶ Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample. RD-32 Docs style ¶ Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09. RD-33 Another project's name or dated history ¶ Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py . Process and test-quality classes ¶ RD-25 Guards no test kills ¶ Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes. RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules ¶ Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?" RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check ¶ Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up). RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule ¶ Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit. RD-19 Template drift ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate. RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI ¶ Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count). CI-only checks (MISRA scan, ESP-IDF, compile-fail) ¶ RD-11 Header outside the library subset ¶ Rule: #include <...> in inc/ and src/ is only from the driver subset of the handbook (KB-CPP-012). #include <numeric> // bad: not in the subset; std::accumulate -> write the OR out #include <string_view> Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt , <string_view> ), tmc5160 (review4 B1, <numeric> ). 2 drivers; the second hit makes it a lint. Detection: lint ( enforced in handbook_check; the preflight must also run the include scan or grep). RD-12 Rule 7.0.3 character arithmetic ¶ Rule: no arithmetic or comparison on a char value, including c - '0' and c == 'x' . int d = c - '0' ; // bad if ( c == 'A' ) {} // bad const int d = DigitValue ( c ); // good: lookup in a constexpr digit array via std::find Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : the bare comparisons too), alicat (review2: about 30 computations predicted; review3 R3-M1, six conversions; m-10, tests), pf1550 (review4 m-4: a template file used in tests). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 7.0.3 (planned): char literals in arithmetic or comparison in inc src tests examples . Until then: grep '.' next to - , + , == , != . RD-13 Rule 8.0.1 missing parentheses ¶ Rule: a binary operand that is itself a binary expression of higher precedence is parenthesised, in static_assert too. static_assert ( kA == 1 && kB < 2 ); // bad static_assert (( kA == 1 ) && ( kB < 2 )); // good Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt , three lines), pf1550 (review4 m-1: static_assert s). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 8.0.1 (planned): parenthesis-depth scan of inc src tests . RD-14 Rule 9.4.1 else-less chain ¶ Rule: every if ... else if chain ends with else , with a comment when empty; in tests and models too. Seen: ads9324 ( reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci3.txt ), tmc5160 (review5 B1: two chains in the model). 3 drivers. Detection: lint : misra_lint rule 9.4.1 (planned). RD-15 Rule 0.1.2 unused return value ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : failInit ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 0.1.2 (planned): a call to a non-void function as an expression statement; mark with an explicit discard where intended. RD-16 Rule 13.3.3 parameter names differ ¶ Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt : checkOxygen ). 1 driver. Detection: lint : rule 13.3.3 (planned): declaration in inc/ against definition in src/*.ipp . RD-17 Rule 7.0.6 literal argument type ¶ Rule: a constant argument has its parameter's type ( _u32 literal), and no mixed-width arithmetic on literals. Seen: ntc (review1 M3), fdo2 (review1 M10), tmc5160 (review1 M7), ws2812 (review1: call sites). 4 drivers. Detection: lint (partial, planned): literal passed to a uint32_t or uint8_t parameter of a known function; review for the rest (the CI scan is final). Question: "Which call passes a bare integer constant to a narrower parameter?" RD-18 Advisories 6.9.2, 15.1.4, 0.0.2 ¶ Rule: these three appear on every driver and need no re-report: 6.9.2 on the unsigned long long literal-operator parameter and on the version getters, 15.1.4 on a constructor whose members have default initialisers, 0.0.2 on a condition a constant-hook port makes always the same. Seen in CI: fdo2, ads9324 ( reports/fdo2-ci-misra.txt , reports/ads9324-ci-misra.txt ); predicted by the reviewer from those runs: pf1550 (review3, review4 m-4), alicat (review3, review4), bno08x (review1). 5 drivers. Detection: lint (planned): the gate compares the CodeQL advisory list to this known list; anything else is new. Reviewers do not report the known three; whether to record them as deviations is an owner decision. RD-20 ESP-IDF REQUIRES incomplete ¶ Rule: every #include of an ESP-IDF header in examples/esp32/main has its component in REQUIRES . Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : esp_timer.h ; the ESP32 job failed in both examples). Later reviews found it clean ( pf1550 review5). 1 driver. Detection: lint (planned): include-to-component map checked against the idf_component_register call. RD-21 ESP32 example cannot start with its defaults ¶ Rule: the example's default pins and Config start up; an optional hook returns true when the pin is absent. Seen: fdo2 (review1 M5), mcp9700 (review1 B-1: GpioSet returned false with the default -1 pin), ntc (review1 M1). 3 drivers. Detection: test : build the ESP32 port against stub ESP headers on the host and run the example's start-up with default Config . review : question "does app_main with the default pins reach the first measurement?" RD-22 Compile-fail regex wording differs by compiler ¶ Rule: an EXPECT: is a concept or type name, or the static_assert text, never compiler wording. Seen: no CI failure yet. Reviewers could not confirm GCC 13/14 and clang CI wording for alicat, pf1550, bno08x (review4, review5, review1). 0 driver hits; listed because it is unverified each time. Detection: lint (planned): every EXPECT: string is static assertion failed , an identifier, or a string from a static_assert . RD-23 Tests are also scanned by MISRA ¶ Rule: the MISRA job builds with tests on, so tests/ , models, fuzz and consumers meet the same rules as inc/ . Seen: tmc5160 (review5 B1, the model), alicat (review3 m-10: char compares in tests and the model, "if CodeQL scans tests"). 2 drivers; whether the job reports test files is not proved by the two CI runs on file. Detection: lint : every misra_lint rule scans tests/ examples/ as well as inc/ src/ .
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.text: The defects that reached an independent reviewer or the first CI run of more than one driver, one entry per class. Review skills cite these ids; the mechanization policy says where each class is caught and when it moves up a level. Append new findings to the entry they belong to, or add an entry (see the policy). Evidence names the driver, the review round ( reviews/<driver>-review<N>.md , finding id) or the CI run ( reports/<driver>-ci-*.txt ). Code examples are generic and minimal; none quotes a datasheet or a standard. Detection levels: lint (a script in the preflight or the gate, no judgement), test (a model knob, a mutation, a fuzz property or a compile-fail case that fails when the defect is present), review (a named reviewer asks one question). Status: enforced is in the template now; planned is the target, tracked in the policy's backlog, and until it lands the level below it (test, then review) is what protects the driver.
docs.title: Recurring defects

docs.title: Index

docs.text: Rule: every way the chip can reset itself is detected from evidence the chip leaves, and no cached value is written over a chip that may have reset. // bad: the chip browned out; shadow_ holds the old setpoint, the chip is at its reset value // bad: writes the whole shadow_ (the stale rest of it) over a chip that may have reset Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { shadow_ . limit = v ; return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( shadow_ )); } // good: check the evidence first, refuse until the application re-initialises Result < void > SetLimit ( uint8_t v ) { if ( auto r = ResetCheck (); ! r ) { return r ; } // status read, sentinel compare; pending until it passes return WriteReg ( kLimit , Pack ( WithLimit ( shadow_ , v ))); } Hurts: stale state rewritten into a chip at reset values energises outputs or sets limits the application never chose; the call returns Ok. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J1), pf1550 (review1 M8, review2 F1, review3 N1, review4 R4-1, review5 R5-2), tmc5160 (review1 M5), fdo2 (review1 B1: abort during start-up leaves the driver initialised). 4 drivers. Detection: test : model knob "reset mid-session" (registers to reset values, reset flags set) plus a fuzz property "no write after a reset is seen"; mutate the sentinel compare and the pending-check latch, each must fail a test. review : hardware-lessons-review 12a. Question: "List every way this chip resets or reloads; for each, which bit or sentinel shows it, which function reads it, and what does a setter do between the reset and that read?"
docs.title: RD-01 Write after an unseen device reset

docs.text: Rule: a read that decides a write, a state change or an identity is validated per the protocol (CRC, echo, length) and a read-modify-write uses only a validated read; a single bad read never clears state or masks a lost write. // bad: one flipped read clears identity, the next switch-off returns NotInitialized and sends nothing if ( ReadReg ( kId ) != kExpectedId ) { identified_ = false ; } // good: two agreeing reads before a state is dropped; switch-off ignores identified_ Hurts: a transient line error becomes "device reset" or "not initialised", a read-modify-write writes garbage bits back, a resync hides a lost write so the chip runs at the wrong current. Seen: pf1550 (review1 B1, M1; review4 R4-3), ads9324 (review1 J2), tmc5160 (review1 M1, lost-write masking by resync), sfm (review1 B1: any NACK after a first sample became DeviceReset), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : model fault "one flipped reply at call k" swept over every call of every public function; the expected result is the call's own error, no state loss, no unsafe write. review : hardware-lessons-review 1, 12. Question: "Which reads in this driver decide something, and is there a mutant that removes each validation?"
docs.title: RD-02 Decision from one unvalidated read

docs.text: Rule: a reply a dead, shorted or floating line can produce (all zeros, all ones, the command echoed, one word repeated) is never a measurement or a ready status. // bad: an all-zero frame has a valid CRC for init 0x00, so 0 degC (or -200 degC after the offset) is returned auto t = DecodeTemperature ( words ); // good: reject by pattern before decoding, then plausibility-check the decoded value if ( IsStuck ( words )) { return Error :: NoDevice ; } Hurts: a wrong value is returned as data, which downstream control trusts. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J3), tmc5160 (review1 M8), sfm (review3 M-A: the temperature path had no stuck check while the sample path had one). 3 drivers. Detection: test : one model fault per pattern (zeros, ones, echo, repeat) applied to every read function; a table test lists each public read function and the fault, so a new read function without a row fails. review : hardware-lessons-review 4. Question: "For each read path, which of the four patterns does the CRC pass, and which line in the code refuses it?"
docs.title: RD-03 Stuck or floating line accepted as data

docs.text: Rule: a call that returns InvalidArgument (or any precondition error) sent nothing and changed nothing; validate first, transfer second. // bad: reads the position first, then rejects the argument auto pos = ReadPos (); if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } // good if ( steps > kMax ) { return Error :: InvalidArgument ; } auto pos = ReadPos (); Hurts: a rejected call moves state or leaves the driver config invalid, and the next call sends from it. Seen: tmc5160 (review1 M2: three sites, found by a fuzz abort), ads9324 (review2 N2: a division by convst_hz before the state check). 2 drivers. Detection: test : the model counts frames; every InvalidArgument test asserts the count is unchanged, and the fuzz target asserts it for every call that returned InvalidArgument . review : hardware-lessons-review 11. Question: "For each early return of an argument error, what is the first line above it that touches the port?"
docs.title: RD-04 Invalid argument still sends something

docs.text: Rule: a switch-off, a release to input and Deinitialize() are never refused for any uncertainty (reset report, failed read, unknown mode, uninitialised after reset) and always send their writes, in the smallest atomic form. // bad Result < void > Off () { if ( ! identified_ ) { return Error :: NotInitialized ; } return Write ( kEnable , 0 ); } // good: acts first, reports after Result < void > Off () { auto r = Write ( kEnable , 0 ); MarkUnverified (); return r ; } Hurts: the one command that makes the system safe is the one that fails when the system is most in doubt. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N1), pf1550 (review2 F2, review3 N2, review4 R4-3), tmc5160 (review3: stop and switch-off refused after a reset report; review1 M4: not verified on UART), alicat (review2 N3: a switch-off in an unknown state is sent only to the held settings). 4 drivers. Detection: test : for every uncertainty flag the driver has, a test sets it through the model and asserts the switch-off still writes (mutation: add the refusal back, the test fails). review : hardware-lessons-review 12c. Question: "Name each flag that can make a call return early; show the test where it is set and Off still sends."
docs.title: RD-05 Stop, switch-off or release refused

docs.text: Rule: buffers handed to the bus are members of the driver object (memory a DMA engine reaches), never locals or function-local statics. // bad Result < void > Read ( Reg r ) { std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx {}; return port_ . Transfer ( tx . data (), rx , 4 ); } // good std :: array < uint8_t , 4 > tx_ {}; // member Hurts: DMA or TCM-stack ports fail on the first frame; the host build and a DMA-disabled example hide it. Seen: ads9324 (review2 N3), pf1550 (review3 N3), bno08x (review1 M-1, UART receive buffers, and the contract said the opposite), tmc5160 (review3 M3; its fix was killed by an address-in-object test, review4). 4 drivers. Alicat keeps its buffers in the bus object (review3). The ads9324 fix still had a survivor that pinned no ownership (review3 m2): the address test below closes that. Detection: test : the mock port records the address of every transmit and receive buffer and asserts it lies inside [&driver, &driver + sizeof(driver)) ; compile it into the shared model. review : KB-HW-019. Question: "In every function that calls the port, where does the memory of each buffer argument live?"
docs.title: RD-06 Transfer buffers on the stack

docs.text: Rule: the model is written from the datasheet, including frame layout, not from the driver; golden frames are transcribed from the datasheet's figures and checked by a test the driver's author did not derive from the code. // bad: driver and model both put the data in bytes 1..2 of the reply, the datasheet says bytes 0..1 of the data word // good: test_model.cpp pins a golden frame copied from the datasheet figure; model includes no driver header Hurts: green tests, wrong data on the wire; only hardware or an independent reader shows it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1: wrong bits of the reply, model and driver agreed), tmc5160 (review5 m2: the model set a status bit the instant the velocity was zero, the chip sets it 2^20 clocks later). 2 drivers. Detection: lint : tests/mock_*.hpp includes no driver header (planned, preflight model-standalone ); review : datasheet-conformance, independence check. Question: "Take one golden frame from the datasheet figure; which test fails if the driver and the model both decode it the other way?"
docs.title: RD-07 Chip model shares the driver's misreading

docs.text: Rule: every command is checked against every state the chip or the driver can be in, including pending timers, power gates, asleep and in-doubt; a start-up that leaves anything pending does not energise. // bad: waits only for velocity == 0, but the chip is still counting a stand-still delay and will drive back while ( Velocity () != 0 ) { } Enable (); // good: also checks the pending-delay flag the datasheet names while ( Velocity () != 0 || DelayActive ()) { } Enable (); Hurts: outputs energise in a state the guard did not consider; the motion or power surprise is real. Seen: tmc5160 (review5 M1: enable during a pending zero-wait), ws2812 (review2 N1: the power gate started open), pf1550 (review1 M3, M4: rail enabled with a voltage no limit checked), sfm (review1 M2: soft reset accepted while asleep), fdo2 (review1 B1). 5 drivers. Detection: test : a generated state x command table test (every public command in every modelled state, expected result and frame count), and a mutant for each guard. review : hardware-lessons-review 11, 12. Question: "Draw the states from the datasheet; for each command and state, where is the guard and which test removes it?"
docs.title: RD-10 Incomplete state-machine guard

docs.text: Rule: bounds, divisors and state are checked before they are used, on every path, including the framing layer. Hurts: abort in hardened builds, UB elsewhere. Seen: bno08x (review1 B-1: a framer returned a frame longer than its buffer), ads9324 (review2 N2: divide before the state check), tmc5160 (review1: fuzz aborts, see RD-04). 3 drivers. Detection: test : libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan in the gate ( enforced ); fuzz target feeds every public function. review : question "which divisor, index or span length comes from a caller or the chip, and where is it checked?"
docs.title: RD-30 Out-of-bounds or UB before a guard

docs.text: Rule: clear-on-read and write-1-to-clear flags collect in one driver-owned latch; a self-check or raw read never discards them. Seen: pf1550 (review1 M2: SelfCheck() and ReadRegister() read status registers the chip clears on read), tmc5160 (review1: Service() cleared the stall event, a BLOCKER, review1 B1). 2 drivers. Detection: test : model with clear-on-read bits; test reads through every diagnostic path, then asserts the latch still reports the fault. review : hardware-lessons-review 10, 12b.
docs.title: RD-31 Clear-on-read flags lost by a diagnostic read

docs.text: Rule: every field position, clear semantic, wait and gap cites its section and has a test that pins it independently. Seen: ads9324 (review1 B1, J4), tmc5160 (review1 B1), sfm (review1 M3, M4), ws2812 (review1 M2, M3), fdo2 (review1 M3, M4). 6 drivers. Detection: review (datasheet-conformance): re-derive the five facts the change touches from the datasheet before reading the code. Question: "For this register or frame, what do the datasheet's bits say, and does the code agree before you look at the model?"
docs.title: RD-28 Datasheet misread in a decode, clear or timing

docs.text: Rule: a reference circuit, wiring table or example never exceeds an absolute maximum or ties a pin the datasheet forbids tying. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M7), fdo2 (review1 M9), ws2812 (review1 M3: documents disagree on the input threshold). 3 drivers. Detection: review : docs and diagram pass. Question: "For each net in the reference circuit, what is the highest voltage the chip pin sees, and where does the datasheet allow it?"
docs.title: RD-29 Hardware doc exceeds a datasheet limit

docs.text: Rule: every behavioural claim in docs, Doxygen, the contract and the build report is checked against the code line that implements it and the test that pins it. /// Enables the bridge again. // doc Result < void > ClearFaults (); // code returns Busy while the motor moves and stays disabled Hurts: callers and later reviewers rely on the claim; a promised error never occurs, a promised recovery never runs. Seen: ws2812 (review1 M5, review2 N2, n9), tmc5160 (review1 M4, review5 m1), fdo2 (review1 M7), pf1550 (review1 M6), bno08x (review1 M-1), ads9324 (review1 J5-J7). 6 drivers. Detection: review via the review-round claims-vs-code check: list every "always", "never", "returns", "enables" in docs and the build report and cite the code line and test for each. Mechanical part ( lint , planned): every Error named in docs exists; every Doxygen @return lists the values the function can return.
docs.title: RD-09 Docs promise behaviour the code lacks

docs.text: Rule: a matrix row, test id or knob named in docs exists in code, and a row's test asserts the row. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J5, J6: 873 rows unproved, fuzz claims invariants it does not check), pf1550 (review2 F4: 47 rows cite symbols that do not exist; F5: knobs that do not exist; review1 M11), ws2812 (review2 n9: "each fix has a test" overstated). 3 drivers. Detection: lint (planned claims-symbols ): every backticked identifier in the datasheet coverage page, the coverage matrix and docs/ambiguities.md resolves with grep in inc/ src/ tests/ . review : row-level sample.
docs.title: RD-08 False coverage matrix or fuzz claim

docs.text: Rule: Markdown lines are at most 120 characters, list items are separated, text changed by a fix is updated everywhere. Seen: ws2812 (review2 n4, n5, n6), ntc (review1), mcp9700 (review2 m2-1). 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced : markdownlint in the preflight; line length 120). Stale text after a change is RD-09.
docs.title: RD-32 Docs style

docs.text: Seen: ntc (review1 M5: old-history wording in eleven places). 1 driver; enforced by tools/check_standalone.py .
docs.title: RD-33 Another project's name or dated history

docs.text: Rule: every guard that protects a write, a state or a value has a test that fails when the guard is removed. Seen: ads9324 (review1 mutants M22 to N66), pf1550 (review2 F3, review3 N4, review4 R4-2: 7 of 12 survivors matter, review5 R5-1), tmc5160 (review1 M6: 22 of 50 survive), bno08x (review1 M-3: 33 survive), alicat (review2, review3). 6 drivers. Detection: test : a mutation runner over the guard lines (one-edit mutants: negate, drop, swap constant), built by the reviewer in each round; target: a template tools/mutate.py run by the gate with a survivor budget of zero on guards. review : the review-round mutant check of fixes.
docs.title: RD-25 Guards no test kills

docs.text: Rule: the fuzz target asserts the invariants of the safety rules (no write after a reset is seen, no switch-on in doubt, no frame after InvalidArgument), and a mutant of each invariant fails it. Seen: ads9324 (review1 J6), pf1550 (review1 M10, review3 N4: blind to a missed reset), alicat (review2 m9, review3 m9: no no-write-in-doubt invariant). 3 drivers. Detection: test : mutate the invariant check in the harness; review : question "which safety rule does the fuzz target assert, and what input would break each?"
docs.title: RD-26 Fuzz target does not check the safety rules

docs.text: Rule: a call in a test or fuzz target takes, as separate arguments, no operation that changes state together with a read of that state ( sent() , Transfers() , pending() , a flag, a counter, a clock). The order of the arguments of a call, of the operands of + - == < and of the two sides of an assignment is unspecified; GCC on x86-64 evaluates arguments right to left, Clang and GCC on aarch64 left to right. Braced-init lists, && , || , ?: and , are sequenced. Two reads of the fuzzer's input ( in.Byte() , FuzzConfig(in) ) in one expression count as well: they advance the input, so the same corpus file decodes into different calls per compiler. // bad: x86-64 GCC reads sent() before the call, so it is always 0 here Check ( d . Write ( v ), was_up , sent ()); // good: the result first, then the read; or pass the probe and read it inside the helper, after the call const auto r = d . Write ( v ); Check ( r , was_up , sent ()); Hurts: the check passes, or aborts, on one CI runner only. A "nothing was sent" promise becomes vacuous, and a positive promise ( sent >= 1 ) aborts on a correct driver; neither shows on an Apple-silicon or aarch64 rehearsal. Seen: dynamixel (first CI, sent >= 1 aborted on x86-64 GCC only), pcal9555 (three fuzz cases, latent), tle92466ed (16 fuzz cases, vacuous; 6 more with two input reads), the template's own fuzz target (5 cases). 3 drivers, all copies of the same pattern. Detection: lint ( enforced ): tools/eval_order_check.py , the eval-order preflight step, scans tests/ and examples/ . test : the fuzz replay with a one-edit mutant that must abort ( mutant_replay_* , kept out of the fuzz_* names so the libFuzzer job does not pick it up).
docs.title: RD-34 Unspecified evaluation order in a test check

docs.text: Seen: sfm (review3 M-B), mcp9700 first push (the ESP32 examples job fails: no such directory). 2 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): the gate runs git ls-files -s | grep ^160000 after setting the pinned commit.
docs.title: RD-24 Missing gitlink for the scripts submodule

docs.text: Seen: fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci2.txt : drift warning and a 160-character workflow line), alicat (review1 m6) and pf1550 (review4 m-3): the template record said unknown . 3 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced ): scaffold.py --check-drift in the gate.
docs.title: RD-19 Template drift

docs.text: Rule: the preflight runs clang-format 20 and clang-tidy over the same file list and compile database as CI, inside the container. Seen: ntc (first CI: tidy failed on a generated file absent from a configure-only database), bno08x (review1 M-2: readability-named-parameter in the install consumer), fdo2 ( reports/fdo2-ci-failed.log : lint job, 2 files), fdo2 later (tidy on the ESP32 stub). 4 drivers. Detection: lint ( enforced in the container preflight once it uses a configure-only database; check the log names the tidy file count).
docs.title: RD-27 Local tidy and format differ from CI

docs.text: Registers ¶ The register map as the driver knows it: 63 entries, their access and the rule for each group. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Register map and reset values: 6 Register Mapping, p. 31 General configuration registers: 6.1 General Configuration Registers, p. 32 Motor driver registers: 6.5 Motor Driver Registers, p. 47 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Access letters: R read, W write-only, RW both, R+WC read and clear by writing 1 (page 31). The coverage map lists every bit field: Coverage map . Group Addresses Registers Driver General 0x00 to 0x0C GCONF, GSTAT, IFCNT, NODECONF, IOIN and OUTPUT, X_COMPARE, OTP_PROG, OTP_READ, FACTORY_CONF, SHORT_CONF, DRV_CONF, GLOBALSCALER, OFFSET_READ SetFlags() , SetDiag() , SetBridge() , SetProtection() , SetCurrent() Velocity dependent 0x10 to 0x15 IHOLD_IRUN, TPOWERDOWN, TSTEP, TPWMTHRS, TCOOLTHRS, THIGH SetCurrent() , SetStandstill() , SetThresholds() Ramp generator 0x20 to 0x36 RAMPMODE, XACTUAL, VACTUAL, VSTART, A1, V1, AMAX, VMAX, DMAX, D1, VSTOP, TZEROWAIT, XTARGET, VDCMIN, SW_MODE, RAMP_STAT, XLATCH SetRamp() , MoveTo() , SetSwitches() Encoder 0x38 to 0x3D ENCMODE, X_ENC, ENC_CONST, ENC_STATUS, ENC_LATCH, ENC_DEVIATION SetEncoder() Microstep table 0x60 to 0x6B MSLUT0 to 7, MSLUTSEL, MSLUTSTART, MSCNT, MSCURACT SetMicrostepTable() Chopper and driver 0x6C to 0x73 CHOPCONF, COOLCONF, DCCTRL, DRV_STATUS, PWMCONF, PWM_SCALE, PWM_AUTO, LOST_STEPS SetChopper() and the rest Reset values ¶ "All registers become reset to 0 upon power up, unless otherwise noted" (page 31). The noted ones: CHOPCONF 0x10410150 , PWMCONF 0xC40C001E , the default microstep table, MSLUTSEL 0xFFFF8056 , MSLUTSTART 0x00F70000 , TPOWERDOWN 10, VSTOP 1, ENC_CONST 0x00010000 , and the OTP-defined fields (A8). Config{} holds them; the shadow starts from them and is rewritten by every EnsureInitialized() . Writes and reads ¶ A write sends the whole 32-bit word from the shadow: there is no read-modify-write over the bus. Reserved bits are written as 0; read-only, forbidden and absent addresses are refused by an address table. A write-only register cannot be read: Refused (A4). The shadow answers instead. ReadRegister(address) reads any readable register; on SPI it costs two transfers. Never written ¶ OTP_PROG, FACTORY_CONF, GCONF.test_mode, and OUTPUT and NODECONF over SPI.

docs.text: Repository setup ¶ The one-time steps an org owner runs after creating a repository from the template, and before the first PR. The scripts are in kokeb-labs/.github/org/ . Each one is a dry run unless given --apply ; --org names the organisation (a driver lives in kokeb-labs-drivers , everything else in kokeb-labs ) and --repo limits it to one repository. The rules behind them are in repo-governance.md . 1. Create and scaffold ¶ gh repo create kokeb-labs-drivers/driver-<chip> --private --template kokeb-labs/driver-template --clone cd driver-<chip> git switch -c feat/initial-driver python3 tools/setup.py tools/setup.py asks for the bus and a one-sentence description, scaffolds, builds and runs the host tests; tools/scaffold.py --help lists every option ( --platforms host,esp32 is a driver's default; a library gets host unless esp32 is asked for); it ends with a checklist of what is left to fill in. 2. Apply the org settings ¶ From a checkout of kokeb-labs/.github , after adding the repository to org/repos.json by PR. Its entry sets the About: the description is the README's first sentence ( C++20 driver for the <vendor> <parts> <what it is> (<bus>) ), and the topics are the shared kokeb-labs driver embedded cpp20 misra-cpp header-only plus the bus, the device category, the vendor and the part ( spi eeprom microchip at25040b ): python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> # the plan python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply # settings, Actions, labels, ... A private repository on the free plan gets the settings, Actions policy and labels; security features and rulesets need it public (the tool says which sections it skips). Run it again, with --check to see that nothing is pending, after the repository goes public (section 6). Run it without --apply first to see what changes. 3. Create the labels ¶ --apply in step 2 already creates them; this is the manual way, for a repository outside the org tool. python3 - <<'PY' import subprocess, yaml for label in yaml.safe_load(open(".github/labels.yml")): subprocess.run(["gh", "label", "create", label["name"], "--color", label["color"], "--description", label["description"], "--force"], check=True) PY 4. Require the gate ¶ After the first CI run has produced the check CI gate / gate , add it to the repository's main-review ruleset as described in The required check . 5. Wire it in ¶ Add the repository as a submodule or CMake dependency where it is consumed, in its own pin PR, then follow checklists/new-driver.md . 6. First release candidate and going public ¶ The order that works, and the reason for each step: main green first. Push, and wait for CI on main , including CI gate / gate . The docs publish to gh-pages from main before any tag does. Triage a failure with the release skill, section 5: re-run the failed jobs only when the infrastructure failed. Tag vX.Y.Z-rc.1 on that commit (the release skill). Its CI repeats the run, then the Release workflow publishes the pre-release: firmware, SBOM, checksums. A pre-release publishes its docs under its own tag and takes latest only when no other version holds it. Make it public ( gh repo edit <org>/<repo> --visibility public --accept-visibility-change-consequences ), then python3 org/kokeb_org.py --org kokeb-labs-drivers --repo driver-<chip> --apply : rulesets, secret scanning with push protection, CodeQL and private vulnerability reporting need a public repository. If the last call answers 422, run it again after a few seconds; the new visibility has not reached that endpoint yet. Enable Pages from the gh-pages branch, root, and open https://<org>.github.io/<repo>/ . --check reports 0 change(s) pending . A private repository on the free plan shares a small Actions storage quota with the rest of its organisation. A full quota fails every upload step in every repository of it at once, which looks like a broken workflow and is not one; a public repository does not count against it.

docs.text: DcStep, encoder and direct mode ¶ The features that go beyond the ramp generator: DcStep, the ABN encoder, direct mode and STEP/DIR. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Encoder registers: 6.4 Encoder Registers, p. 45 STEP/DIR interface and MicroPlyer: 15 STEP/DIR Interface, p. 94 DcStep: 17 DcStep, p. 99 ABN incremental encoder interface: 20 ABN Incremental Encoder Interface, p. 107 DC motor and direct mode: 21 DC Motor or Solenoid, p. 110 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . DcStep ¶ SetDcStep() writes VDCMIN and DCCTRL. DcStep needs the default microstep table, high_fullstep and high_const_off set, TOFF 3 or more and DC_TIME above the blank time, otherwise InvalidArgument . VDCMIN is 0 (off) or 256 and up, with bits 7..0 ignored by the chip (A27). ReadLostSteps() returns LOST_STEPS (section 17, page 99). Encoder ¶ SetEncoder() writes ENCMODE, ENC_CONST and ENC_DEVIATION when Encoder::declared . The constant is units::EncoderScaleFor(steps_per_rev, counts_per_rev, ...) : binary or decimal, with the sign rule of page 107 for negative decimal constants (A43). ReadEncoderPosition() , SetEncoderPosition() , ReadEncoderLatch() , ReadEncoderStatus() and ClearEncoderEvents() cover the registers; the deviation warning latches in ENC_STATUS. In STEP/DIR mode the encoder pins change function and the calls return Unsupported . Direct mode ¶ Direct mode takes the coil currents (or PWM) from XTARGET (section 21, page 110). It needs Ack::DirectMode ; EnterDirectMode() is refused while the motor moves, and SetDirectCurrents() limits the values to the range of the chopper mode. ExitDirectMode() holds, clears the mode and writes XTARGET = XACTUAL so the motor does not jump (A26). STEP/DIR ¶ With SD_MODE high the chip takes STEP and DIR from pins and MicroPlyer interpolates to 256 microsteps. The serial interface still configures the chip; the ramp, the encoder and direct mode are unavailable. DIAG outputs change their function ( DIAG and status ). Microstep table ¶ Microstep table explains SetMicrostepTable() .

docs.text: SPI protocol ¶ The 40-bit datagram, the pipelined read, the status byte, write verification and the daisy chain. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: SPI datagram, status byte and timing: 4 SPI Interface, p. 23 SPI daisy chain: 4.1 SPI Datagram Structure, p. 23 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Datagram ¶ Every transfer is 40 bits, MSB first, with CSN low for the whole datagram: one address byte (the write flag in bit 7 and a seven-bit address), then 32 data bits (section 4.1, page 23). The reply has the same shape: the SPI status byte, then 32 data bits. Bit Status byte (section 4.1.2, page 24) 7 status_stop_r 6 status_stop_l 5 position_reached 4 velocity_reached 3 standstill 2 sg2 1 driver_error (GSTAT bit 1) 0 reset_flag (GSTAT bit 0) Pipelined reads ¶ A read takes two datagrams: the first carries the address, the second returns the data (and may carry anything, so the driver sends another read of the same address). After a write, the next reply mirrors the data just written. The datasheet's worked example is replayed by the tests: reading XACTUAL sends 0x2100000000 twice; writing VMAX 0xA700ABCDEF returns the status byte and the previous read data. The status byte is latched at the end of an access and shown with the next transfer, so it is one transfer old (A3). The driver never acts on a status byte as a result of the same call. Mode 3 ¶ The chip samples on the rising edge of SCK, with SCK idle high: SPI mode 3 (section 4.3, page 25; A1). The port's SckHz() hook, when present, is checked against 4 MHz on the internal clock or fCLK / 2 with an external one, with a 10 percent margin (A2). The examples run at 1 MHz. A transfer of any other length than 5 bytes per chip is not committed by the chip; a clock that never idles high shifts garbage, which the version check at start-up turns into DeviceIdMismatch . Write verification ¶ Verify Extra traffic Detects None none nothing Echo one transfer the next reply must mirror the data just written ReadBack one or two transfers a readable register that differs from the write Counter UART only IFCNT counted the write Verification is per call, with a trailing Verify argument. SPI has no integrity check on the wire: a corrupted reply looks like data. Enable() reads GSTAT to catch a brown-out reset that happened since start-up, but a corrupted GSTAT reply can hide the flag; call Service() periodically. Daisy chain ¶ With chain_length n and chain_index k (0 is the chip whose SDI is on MOSI, A34), a transfer is 5n bytes and this chip's 5 bytes sit at offset 5 * (n - 1 - k) . Every other slot carries a read of GCONF, which changes nothing. Several TMC5160 objects share one port object. // Three chips in one chain: index 0 is the chip whose SDI is on MOSI. tmc5160 :: Error StartChain ( MyPort & port ) { tmc5160 :: Config config = tmc5160 :: MakeConfig ( tmc5160 :: Motor {. rated_rms_ma = 1000 , . coil_resistance_mohm = 6000 }, tmc5160 :: Board {. rsense_mohm = 100 , . supply_mv = 24'000 }); config . spi . chain_length = 3 ; static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > chip_a ( port , [ & ] { auto c = config ; c . spi . chain_index = 0 ; return c ; }()); static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > chip_b ( port , [ & ] { auto c = config ; c . spi . chain_index = 1 ; return c ; }()); if ( auto r = chip_a . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { return r . error ; } return chip_b . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // every transfer is 15 bytes: 5 per chip } Stuck lines ¶ A MISO held low or high reads as a status byte and data of all zeros or all ones. At start-up both fail the version check ( DeviceIdMismatch ). Later, all ones has the reset flag set and the driver reports UnexpectedReset ; all zeros looks like valid data with no flags. Service() , ReadSnapshot() , ReadDriverStatus() , ReadStallGuard() and the standstill check therefore read IOIN when every word and the status byte are 0: a VERSION other than 0x30 is Bus , a right one is a live chip that has no flag set at that moment. A single read of any other register is not checked. A floating MISO reads as either. Stuck and floating lines are open work for hardware verification.
