docs.text: Every transfer is 40 bits, MSB first, with CSN low for the whole datagram: one address byte (the write flag in bit 7 and a seven-bit address), then 32 data bits (section 4.1, page 23). The reply has the same shape: the SPI status byte, then 32 data bits. Bit Status byte (section 4.1.2, page 24) 7 status_stop_r 6 status_stop_l 5 position_reached 4 velocity_reached 3 standstill 2 sg2 1 driver_error (GSTAT bit 1) 0 reset_flag (GSTAT bit 0)
docs.title: Datagram

docs.text: A read takes two datagrams: the first carries the address, the second returns the data (and may carry anything, so the driver sends another read of the same address). After a write, the next reply mirrors the data just written. The datasheet's worked example is replayed by the tests: reading XACTUAL sends 0x2100000000 twice; writing VMAX 0xA700ABCDEF returns the status byte and the previous read data. The status byte is latched at the end of an access and shown with the next transfer, so it is one transfer old (A3). The driver never acts on a status byte as a result of the same call.
docs.title: Pipelined reads

docs.text: The chip samples on the rising edge of SCK, with SCK idle high: SPI mode 3 (section 4.3, page 25; A1). The port's SckHz() hook, when present, is checked against 4 MHz on the internal clock or fCLK / 2 with an external one, with a 10 percent margin (A2). The examples run at 1 MHz. A transfer of any other length than 5 bytes per chip is not committed by the chip; a clock that never idles high shifts garbage, which the version check at start-up turns into DeviceIdMismatch .
docs.title: Mode 3

docs.text: Verify Extra traffic Detects None none nothing Echo one transfer the next reply must mirror the data just written ReadBack one or two transfers a readable register that differs from the write Counter UART only IFCNT counted the write Verification is per call, with a trailing Verify argument. SPI has no integrity check on the wire: a corrupted reply looks like data. Enable() reads GSTAT to catch a brown-out reset that happened since start-up, but a corrupted GSTAT reply can hide the flag; call Service() periodically.
docs.title: Write verification

docs.text: With chain_length n and chain_index k (0 is the chip whose SDI is on MOSI, A34), a transfer is 5n bytes and this chip's 5 bytes sit at offset 5 * (n - 1 - k) . Every other slot carries a read of GCONF, which changes nothing. Several TMC5160 objects share one port object. // Three chips in one chain: index 0 is the chip whose SDI is on MOSI. tmc5160 :: Error StartChain ( MyPort & port ) { tmc5160 :: Config config = tmc5160 :: MakeConfig ( tmc5160 :: Motor {. rated_rms_ma = 1000 , . coil_resistance_mohm = 6000 }, tmc5160 :: Board {. rsense_mohm = 100 , . supply_mv = 24'000 }); config . spi . chain_length = 3 ; static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > chip_a ( port , [ & ] { auto c = config ; c . spi . chain_index = 0 ; return c ; }()); static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyPort > chip_b ( port , [ & ] { auto c = config ; c . spi . chain_index = 1 ; return c ; }()); if ( auto r = chip_a . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { return r . error ; } return chip_b . EnsureInitialized (). error ; // every transfer is 15 bytes: 5 per chip }
docs.title: Daisy chain

docs.text: A MISO held low or high reads as a status byte and data of all zeros or all ones. At start-up both fail the version check ( DeviceIdMismatch ). Later, all ones has the reset flag set and the driver reports UnexpectedReset ; all zeros looks like valid data with no flags. Service() , ReadSnapshot() , ReadDriverStatus() , ReadStallGuard() and the standstill check therefore read IOIN when every word and the status byte are 0: a VERSION other than 0x30 is Bus , a right one is a live chip that has no flag set at that moment. A single read of any other register is not checked. A floating MISO reads as either. Stuck and floating lines are open work for hardware verification.
docs.title: Stuck lines

docs.text: StallGuard2 and CoolStep ¶ Load measurement, stall detection and the load-adaptive current. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Reference switches and SW_MODE: 6.3 Ramp Generator Registers, p. 43 CoolStep and StallGuard2 registers: 6.5 Motor Driver Registers, p. 53 StallGuard2: 13 StallGuard2 Load Measurement, p. 87 Homing with StallGuard: 13.4 Homing with StallGuard, p. 90 CoolStep: 14 CoolStep Operation, p. 91 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . StallGuard2 ¶ SetStallGuard() writes the threshold SGT (-64 to 63) and the filter. ReadStallGuard() returns the 10-bit SG_RESULT. StallGuard2 is valid only above the velocity set in TCOOLTHRS, so Thresholds::cool must be set first; the driver enforces that for SetStopOnStall() too. The value depends on the motor, the supply and the speed: tune SGT on the machine (section 13.1, page 88). // StallGuard2 with a stop on stall. The motor stays stopped until ReleaseStall(). tmc5160 :: Error SensorlessStop ( Motor & motor ) { if ( auto r = motor . SetThresholds ( tmc5160 :: Thresholds {. cool = 200'000 }); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . SetStallGuard ( tmc5160 :: StallGuard {. threshold = 4 , . filter = true }); ! r ) { return r . error ; } if ( auto r = motor . SetStopOnStall ( true ); ! r ) { return r . error ; } const auto ramp = motor . ReadRampStatus (); if ( ramp && ramp . value . event_stop_stall ) { return motor . ReleaseStall (). error ; // clear the event: the motor may move again } return ramp . error ; } Stop on stall ¶ With SetStopOnStall(true) the ramp generator stops when the chip reports a stall; RAMP_STAT.event_stop_sg latches the event. The motor does not restart by itself: ReleaseStall() holds, verifies standstill, clears the event, and only then may a new move start (section 13.4, page 90). A soft stop together with stop on stall is refused. Switching the stop off ( SetStopOnStall(false) , or SetSwitches() without stop_left or stop_right ) would make the chip continue towards the old target (pages 43, 44, 90). When the matching event is latched, the driver therefore reads RAMP_STAT first and ends the ramp at the present position (position mode, XTARGET = XACTUAL) before it writes SW_MODE. The latched event itself stays until ReleaseStall() . A start-up does the same for a ramp or a stall stop left by the last session ( BeginReport::stall_latched tells). CoolStep ¶ SetCoolStep() writes SEMIN, SEMAX, SEUP, SEDN and the minimum current. SEMIN 0 turns CoolStep off. CoolStep lowers the current between IRUN and half (or a quarter) of IRUN when the load allows; it needs StallGuard2 to be valid, so TCOOLTHRS applies (section 14.2, page 91). Limits of the measurement ¶ StallGuard2 is not reliable at very low speed or with StealthChop; DcStep and CoolStep affect it. The driver exposes the raw values and does not interpret them (A38).

docs.text: Testing and CI ¶ How the driver is checked: host tests against an independent model of the chip, a fuzzer that corrupts what the chip sends back, compiled documentation, an install test, ESP32 and Cortex-M builds, static analysis and measured quality gates, on every pull request. None of it has run on a chip. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: UART CRC-8: 5.2 CRC Calculation, p. 28 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Host tests ¶ The tests build the real driver against a model of the TMC5160 ( tests/mock_tmc5160.hpp ): the register file with its reset values and write-only registers, the ramp generator (in physical units, with its own arithmetic), the sequencer and microstep counter, StallGuard2 and short, overtemperature and charge-pump injection, the reference switches, the encoder, DIAG outputs, the SPI front end (pipelined reads, status byte, daisy chain) and the UART front end (frames, CRC, IFCNT, SENDDELAY, 12-bit recovery). The bus layer ( tests/mock_tmc5160_bus.hpp ) fails one transfer, every transfer from some index, corrupts a reply, drops a UART reply, or holds the line at one level. They build with the firmware's flags, -fno-exceptions -fno-rtti , and warnings as errors, on GCC and Clang. cmake -S . -B build -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON cmake --build build ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure File Covers tests/test_lifecycle.cpp Construction, EnsureInitialized() , strap and version checks, Enable() , Disable() , ClearFaults() and the fault paths tests/test_bus.cpp SPI framing and chain, UART framing, CRC, IFCNT, recovery, node programming, write verification, the datasheet vectors tests/test_current.cpp The current plan, the ceiling, the sense-resistor bound, the write order of SetCurrent() tests/test_motion.cpp The ramp registers, moves, stops, switches, homing primitives, StealthChop sequencing, StallGuard2, CoolStep, DcStep, encoder, direct mode tests/test_core.cpp Validate() as a mutation table of invalid and valid configurations, the units, the microstep table, the registers tests/test_stops.cpp How motion ends and when the bridge may be energised again: the stop after a failed start-up, the switch-off ramp stop, the TZEROWAIT pause, and the read order of the standstill check against a chip that runs on while each transfer is on the line ( Wire::xfer_us ) tests/test_scenarios.cpp Whole sessions over both buses: start-up, motion, fault, brown-out, recovery tests/test_knobs.cpp One test per ambiguity knob ( Ambiguities ) tests/test_kconfig.cpp KconfigDefaults() with and without CONFIG_ values tests/test_version.cpp The version getters follow the generated header tests/fuzz/ The fuzz target; CTest replays its corpus ( tmc5160_fuzz_tmc5160_corpus ), see below tests/compile_fail/ Code that must not compile, each for its EXPECT: diagnostic: a port without DelayUs() , a void GpioSet() , a wrong GpioGet() level type, a DelayUs(uint16_t) , an SckHz() that is not const , an Exchange() with a narrowed parameter, a port with both buses, a hook without noexcept , an invalid CheckedConfig , a class that is not a port tests/docs/ Every code block of this site, compiled examples/host/ Eleven host examples, built with the test flags and run ( tmc5160_host_<name> ) tests/check_install.cmake Installs into a scratch prefix and builds tests/install_consumer/ with find_package(tmc5160) tests/check_doxygen.cmake Doxygen with _config/Doxyfile and warnings as errors, when doxygen is installed The model stands alone ¶ The model is written from the datasheet, not from the driver: it does not include tmc5160_registers.hpp or tmc5160_types.hpp . Its register addresses (namespace tmc5160_test::m ), field masks, reset values, ramp arithmetic and CRC-8 are its own, so a wrong constant in the driver cannot hide behind the same wrong constant in the model (handbook KB-TST-030). The datasheet's own vectors are test cases: the seven CRC datagrams of page 116, the SPI worked example of page 24, the microstep table formula of page 49 and the encoder constants of page 108. Every behaviour that was ambiguous in the datasheet is a switch of the model ( Ambiguities ), so a test runs the driver against each reading. The model is behavioural: it does not claim a bit-exact trajectory (A22). Fuzz tests ¶ Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_tmc5160.cpp lets libFuzzer choose the bus (SPI or UART), then up to 30 driver operations, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits, replace the reply or corrupt the request. Between calls it changes the chip: the version, the strap, a short, an overtemperature, a stall, the reference switches, a brown-out. After every call it checks sixteen invariants and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks. Among them: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer, and InvalidArgument means nothing was sent; the model's coil current never exceeded the rated current (F8): on SPI, which has no integrity check, a brown-out followed by a corrupted read is exempt, and the limitation is documented; the driver is never enabled without being initialised, and a latched fault implies initialisation; read-only and forbidden registers are never written, and OTP_PROG and FACTORY_CONF never reach the chip; UnexpectedReset leaves the driver uninitialised; a refusal never leaves the bridge on above the rating (F13), and a start-up that failed after its first write leaves the driver off and not started, and TOFF 0 in the chip unless the error is a bus error (F14); Deinitialize() always leaves the driver uninitialised, and ProgramNode() on SPI is Unsupported ; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DTMC5160_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_tmc5160 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_tmc5160 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tmc5160 The same file also builds without libFuzzer, and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tmc5160/ on GCC and Clang ( tmc5160_fuzz_tmc5160_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. The fuzzer found three real hazards during development (a brown-out followed by Enable() , lost UART writes, and a failure between the two current writes); each is now a test. Mutation check ¶ The review of this driver ran fifty hand-made faults (an operator, a shift, a deleted guard) against the tests; the tests in tests/test_mutants.cpp and the strengthened older ones kill every one of them except three that cannot be observed: GCONF test mode (the bit is never reachable from a Config ), the SPI refusal of NODECONF (the address is refused earlier, in the argument check) and the MoveTo() ramp-written check (start-up always writes the ramp). A fourth, a wrong RAMP_STAT clear mask, is now a static_assert that ties the mask to the register table. Six more faults found while fixing the review (the stall-clear mask, the reset gate, the counter resync, the off-verify, the direct-mode target and the stuck-line check) are killed too. The standstill check of Enable() is one RAMP_STAT read (vzero and t_zerowait_active); T257 polls it against a chip that runs on while each transfer is on the line ( Wire::xfer_us ) and kills a missing vzero check and a missing t_zerowait_active check. The order of the motion writes is tested the same way: T258 to T260 ( MoveTo() after a stop or a switch-off, Stop(HoldTarget) and the start-up stop, RunVelocity() from a move the other way) and the timed part of T256 (the switch-off stop with the mode in doubt) kill each old write order. T261 kills the removal of any word from the stuck-line checks of Service() , ReadSnapshot() , ReadDriverStatus() and ReadStallGuard() , and the IOIN.VERSION tie-break; T265 a failed IOIN read. The model's position mode keeps its moving direction while it stops, so a stop overshoots the target and runs back as the chip does (page 83 c). T262 sweeps the start-up stop with TZEROWAIT 0 and kills a standstill check without position_reached; T263 kills one that asks for it outside position mode or with VMAX 0. T264 ( MoveTo() from velocity mode and the VSTART restore), T266 ( SetHomePosition() order) and T267 ( RunVelocity() from a running position move) are timed too. T268 ( RunVelocity() during the pause of a HoldTarget stop) and T277 (during the overshoot of one, TZEROWAIT 0) kill the speed-first order from position mode and an extra VACTUAL read there; T279 compares the measured run-back with the documented bound for five ramps (V1 0; MoveConfig(0); VSTART below V1; VSTART above V1; A1 above AMAX below V1, so A1 and AMAX are told apart); T280 kills the mode first from hold mode at rest (a burst at the old VMAX); T281 pins the write order for every starting mode (same velocity mode, other velocity mode, position mode, hold mode both ways), so the latency-only orders are killed too; T271 kills an ignored read failure from hold mode, T272 a missing read from hold mode and VMAX before VSTART on a start from rest, T278 and T282 the VSTART bounds of SetMaxVelocity() (the chip's and the profile's) and a MoveTo() with VMAX 0; T284 a failed SetMaxVelocity() that would change the kept VMAX; T285 a MoveBy() that reads before it refuses. T276 (a TZEROWAIT pause after a VMAX 0 stop and after an arrival is Busy) kills a missing t_zerowait_active check. The model is checked by T269 (the run-back of a HoldTarget stop), T270 (two-phase deceleration), T274 (velocity mode passes through 0 at AMAX), T275 (every legal position move reaches its target) and T283 (a lower VMAX is followed with AMAX; no VSTOP in velocity mode). The run is a throwaway script, not part of CI. Quality gates ¶ The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 60 to 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( tmc5160_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/tmc5160.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published. Documentation snippets ¶ Every C++ block on this site is included from tests/docs/ , which the host build compiles (target tmc5160_doc_snippets ) with the driver instantiated over the documented port. A change to the API that breaks a page breaks the build first. The README's example is a generated copy of the same file; kokeb-docs check fails when it drifts. CI workflows ¶ Everything runs from ci.yml , which calls one workflow file per check and ends in the CI gate job, the single required check ( CI gate / gate ). Job What it checks Host tests GCC, then Clang (one job), build and run every test above, then build and run examples/host on its own Host quality The gates above: complexity, coverage, sanitizers, fuzzing Cross-compile arm-none-eabi-g++ for Cortex-M0+, M4F and M7F with the strict flags, warnings as errors (nothing linked) C++ lint clang-format and clang-tidy over the sources MISRA MISRA C++:2023 and the C++20 profile on traced host and Cortex-M builds, at level high (see Quality gates ) Docs Strict site build ( _config/mkdocs.yml ), figure and generated-region drift, Doxygen ( _config/Doxyfile ), offline link check, Lighthouse Repository checks One job: DCO on pull requests, the org standard, Markdown and YAML lint, the Kokeb Labs handbook rules for .kokeb/handbook.yml (by rule ID), template drift (warns only) and cppcheck over the driver sources; a second job runs the handbook's source checks (include guards, bus requirements, raw access) CI gate Passes only if every job above passed: the one required check The ESP32 examples job builds every app in examples/esp32/app_config.yml , for each listed ESP-IDF version and build type, with the repository root as the driver's component, and lints the example sources. The gate needs it too. The workflows call the shared, versioned workflows of kokeb-labs/ci-tools at @v1 . On hardware ¶ Nothing in this repository has run on a chip. An MCU example ( Examples ) is the bench test: it moves the motor one revolution each way and logs the position. The bench steps that confirm each decision of Ambiguities are open work. Record the board and the result in the pull request's bench-status section.

The model is behavioural: it does not claim a bit-exact trajectory (A22).
docs.title: The model stands alone

docs.text: Everything the driver reads comes from the chip over the bus, so the data read is what a noisy cable, a wrong part or a broken chip controls. tests/fuzz/fuzz_tmc5160.cpp lets libFuzzer choose the bus (SPI or UART), then up to 30 driver operations, and on every transfer what the bus does: pass it to the model, fail it, flip bits, replace the reply or corrupt the request. Between calls it changes the chip: the version, the strap, a short, an overtemperature, a stall, the reference switches, a brown-out. After every call it checks sixteen invariants and aborts, naming the line, when one breaks. Among them: a failed call returns an Error the enum defines; before EnsureInitialized() no call makes a transfer, and InvalidArgument means nothing was sent; the model's coil current never exceeded the rated current (F8): on SPI, which has no integrity check, a brown-out followed by a corrupted read is exempt, and the limitation is documented; the driver is never enabled without being initialised, and a latched fault implies initialisation; read-only and forbidden registers are never written, and OTP_PROG and FACTORY_CONF never reach the chip; UnexpectedReset leaves the driver uninitialised; a refusal never leaves the bridge on above the rating (F13), and a start-up that failed after its first write leaves the driver off and not started, and TOFF 0 in the chip unless the error is a bus error (F14); Deinitialize() always leaves the driver uninitialised, and ProgramNode() on SPI is Unsupported ; every log line is a non-empty plain-text message. # libFuzzer needs Clang (on macOS, Homebrew's LLVM) cmake -S . -B build-fuzz -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON -DTMC5160_BUILD_FUZZERS = ON cmake --build build-fuzz --target fuzz_tmc5160 ./build-fuzz/tests/fuzz/fuzz_tmc5160 -max_total_time = 120 tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tmc5160 The same file also builds without libFuzzer, and CTest replays every input in tests/fuzz/corpus/fuzz_tmc5160/ on GCC and Clang ( tmc5160_fuzz_tmc5160_corpus ): the seeds, and every input that ever broke a promise (name it regress-* ), so a fixed bug stays fixed. The fuzzer found three real hazards during development (a brown-out followed by Enable() , lost UART writes, and a failure between the two current writes); each is now a test.
docs.title: Fuzz tests

docs.text: The review of this driver ran fifty hand-made faults (an operator, a shift, a deleted guard) against the tests; the tests in tests/test_mutants.cpp and the strengthened older ones kill every one of them except three that cannot be observed: GCONF test mode (the bit is never reachable from a Config ), the SPI refusal of NODECONF (the address is refused earlier, in the argument check) and the MoveTo() ramp-written check (start-up always writes the ramp). A fourth, a wrong RAMP_STAT clear mask, is now a static_assert that ties the mask to the register table. Six more faults found while fixing the review (the stall-clear mask, the reset gate, the counter resync, the off-verify, the direct-mode target and the stuck-line check) are killed too. The standstill check of Enable() is one RAMP_STAT read (vzero and t_zerowait_active); T257 polls it against a chip that runs on while each transfer is on the line ( Wire::xfer_us ) and kills a missing vzero check and a missing t_zerowait_active check. The order of the motion writes is tested the same way: T258 to T260 ( MoveTo() after a stop or a switch-off, Stop(HoldTarget) and the start-up stop, RunVelocity() from a move the other way) and the timed part of T256 (the switch-off stop with the mode in doubt) kill each old write order. T261 kills the removal of any word from the stuck-line checks of Service() , ReadSnapshot() , ReadDriverStatus() and ReadStallGuard() , and the IOIN.VERSION tie-break; T265 a failed IOIN read. The model's position mode keeps its moving direction while it stops, so a stop overshoots the target and runs back as the chip does (page 83 c). T262 sweeps the start-up stop with TZEROWAIT 0 and kills a standstill check without position_reached; T263 kills one that asks for it outside position mode or with VMAX 0. T264 ( MoveTo() from velocity mode and the VSTART restore), T266 ( SetHomePosition() order) and T267 ( RunVelocity() from a running position move) are timed too. T268 ( RunVelocity() during the pause of a HoldTarget stop) and T277 (during the overshoot of one, TZEROWAIT 0) kill the speed-first order from position mode and an extra VACTUAL read there; T279 compares the measured run-back with the documented bound for five ramps (V1 0; MoveConfig(0); VSTART below V1; VSTART above V1; A1 above AMAX below V1, so A1 and AMAX are told apart); T280 kills the mode first from hold mode at rest (a burst at the old VMAX); T281 pins the write order for every starting mode (same velocity mode, other velocity mode, position mode, hold mode both ways), so the latency-only orders are killed too; T271 kills an ignored read failure from hold mode, T272 a missing read from hold mode and VMAX before VSTART on a start from rest, T278 and T282 the VSTART bounds of SetMaxVelocity() (the chip's and the profile's) and a MoveTo() with VMAX 0; T284 a failed SetMaxVelocity() that would change the kept VMAX; T285 a MoveBy() that reads before it refuses. T276 (a TZEROWAIT pause after a VMAX 0 stop and after an arrival is Busy) kills a missing t_zerowait_active check. The model is checked by T269 (the run-back of a HoldTarget stop), T270 (two-phase deceleration), T274 (velocity mode passes through 0 at AMAX), T275 (every legal position move reaches its target) and T283 (a lower VMAX is followed with AMAX; no VSTOP in velocity mode). The run is a throwaway script, not part of CI.

docs.text: The Host quality job measures the library code, inc/ and src/ only (tests and examples are left out), and fails when a value is over the limits of this repository's assurance level, high (set in .kokeb/handbook.yml , defined by the handbook's ADR-0020): Gate Tool and how it is measured Limit at high Complexity lizard 1.24.1, modified cyclomatic complexity ( -m : a switch counts once) per function CCN at most 15 Function length lizard, lines of code per function at most 60 Parameters lizard, per function at most 6 Line coverage GCC 14 --coverage -O0 , every CTest, gcovr 8.7 --merge-lines (a template's lines count once across its instances), --exclude-unreachable-branches --exclude-throw-branches at least 85 % Branch coverage same run at least 75 % MC/DC GCC -fcondition-coverage , same run measured, not gated at high (100 % at safety ) Sanitizers Clang, -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all , every CTest no report Fuzzing libFuzzer with ASan and UBSan, 60 to 120 s per target no broken promise The reports are in the run's host-quality-reports artifact and its step summary. To run the gates locally: # Coverage (GCC 14 or later), then the complexity limits cmake -S . -B build-cov -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = g++-14 -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "--coverage -O0 -fcondition-coverage" cmake --build build-cov && ctest --test-dir build-cov gcovr --root . --filter inc/ --filter src/ --merge-lines --exclude-unreachable-branches --txt build-cov lizard -m -C 15 -L 60 -a 6 inc src # Sanitizers (Clang) cmake -S . -B build-san -DCMAKE_CXX_COMPILER = clang++ -DTMC5160_BUILD_TESTS = ON \ -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS = "-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all -O1 -g" cmake --build build-san && ctest --test-dir build-san --output-on-failure The fuzz gate runs locally as shown in Fuzz tests . clang-tidy 20 ( _config/.clang-tidy : bugprone, CERT, clang-analyzer, cppcoreguidelines, modernize, performance, portability and readability, each disabled check with its reason) and cppcheck (strict) run in the C++ lint and Repository checks jobs and fail on any finding. The MISRA job ( ci-misra.yml ) runs the shared ru-misra workflow of ci-tools at level high : it traces a host build and the Cortex-M build ( tmc5160_optimised_build ) of every translation unit, checks them against MISRA C++:2023 and the handbook's C++20 profile (the CodeQL coding-standards and profile packs, plus the validated clang-tidy and cppcheck checks), and reports each finding against the handbook's compliance matrix and deviation records. A finding is fixed in the code; a deliberate exception names its deviation on the line before it ( // codeql::misra_deviation_next_line(MD-CPP-009) above the .ipp include of inc/tmc5160.hpp ). Until the repository is public the job runs with open_source_prerelease: true , the declaration that the code is released under the licence in LICENSE and is to be published.

docs.text: Troubleshooting ¶ Symptoms, causes and fixes, cheapest check first. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: Global status and interface counter: 6.1 General Configuration Registers, p. 33 Power-up reset: 25 Power-Up Reset, p. 119 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . EnsureInitialized returns InvalidArgument ¶ The configuration failed Validate() before any byte was sent. Config{} is not valid: build it with MakeConfig() from the declared motor, the sense resistor and the supply. Check the rated current against the sense resistor ( Current and limits ). EnsureInitialized returns Bus ¶ The port reported a failure: EnsureInitialized() returned false or a transfer did. Check the bus pins in the port, and with a logic analyser that the first datagram appears on the bus. EnsureInitialized returns DeviceIdMismatch ¶ IOIN.VERSION did not read 0x30 . Symptom Likely cause Fix All zeros MISO not connected, CSN not reaching the chip, or no VCC_IO Check continuity and the supply All ones MISO floating high, or an unpowered chip Check VCC_IO and the pull-up Wrong data SPI mode other than 3, or CSN released inside a datagram Use mode 3; keep CSN low for the whole 40 bits EnsureInitialized returns ModeMismatch ¶ The SD_MODE or SPI_MODE strap, as read from IOIN, does not match Config::mode or the bus. Fix the strap, or the configuration ( Hardware ). UART reads return Timeout ¶ No reply came back. Check that TX and RX are joined on one wire with a series resistor, that the node address matches SLAVEADDR (the node is selected by the NAI/NAO chain, UART protocol ), and that the baud rate is inside the chip's autodetect range. Raise SENDDELAY when several nodes share the wire. UART reads return Crc ¶ A reply was corrupted. Reads are retried twice; a persisting Crc points at the wire, a missing common ground or a baud rate the chip mis-detects. Enable returns UnexpectedReset ¶ GSTAT.reset was set: the chip reset since start-up, usually a supply dip on VCC_IO. The write-only registers are lost and the driver is uninitialised; EnsureInitialized() rewrites everything. Enable returns DeviceFault ¶ GSTAT.drv_err is set: a short to ground or an overtemperature shutdown. Remove the cause, wait for the chip to cool, then ClearFaults() and Enable() again. Enable returns VerifyFailed (UART) ¶ The interface counter IFCNT does not match the number of writes the driver sent: a write was lost on the wire. Check the wire, then EnsureInitialized() . A setter returns LimitExceeded or Refused ¶ The request exceeds the declared motor, the 5 % current margin or a ramp limit, or a guard needs an acknowledgement. Read the call's page: Current and limits , Guards . The motor does not move ¶ Is the power stage on? Enable() and the DRV_ENN level. Is the motor current non-zero? SetCurrent() and the realised currents it returns. Is the ramp programmed? VMAX and AMAX of zero do not move ( Motion ). Is the mode right? In STEP/DIR mode the ramp calls return Unsupported . Did a stall stop it? ReleaseStall() . The motor is noisy or loses steps ¶ Tune the chopper ( Chopper ) and the StealthChop velocity threshold; check StallGuard and CoolStep thresholds ( StallGuard and CoolStep ).

docs.text: UART protocol ¶ The single wire UART datagram, the CRC-8, the interface counter, node addressing and error recovery. Datasheet sections this page relies on From Analog Devices (Trinamic) TMC5160A-DS 1.18: UART datagram, node address and SENDDELAY: 5.1 Datagram Structure, p. 26 UART CRC-8: 5.2 CRC Calculation, p. 28 Addressing multiple UART nodes: 5.4 Addressing Multiple Nodes, p. 29 All of them, with the driver API for each: Datasheet map . Datagram ¶ Eight bits, no parity, one stop bit, least significant bit first. Each datagram starts with the sync nibble 1010 , so byte 0 is 0x05 , then the node address, the register address with the write flag, four data bytes (high byte first) and a CRC-8 (section 5.1, page 26). Frame Bytes Content Write 8 sync, node, 0x80 OR register, data[4], CRC Read request 4 sync, node, register, CRC Read reply 8 sync, 0xFF , register, data[4], CRC The chip detects the baud rate from the sync nibble of every datagram: 9000 baud at the lowest, up to fCLK / 16 . A gap of more than 63 bit times between start bits resets the receiver; after an error the line must stay idle for at least 12 bit times (page 26). The driver waits 12 bit times at the declared baud after a failed exchange (A33). CRC-8 ¶ The polynomial is x^8 + x^2 + x + 1 ( 0x07 ), the initial value 0, bits LSB first, over every byte before the CRC (section 5.2, page 28). The seven example datagrams of page 116 (CRC 0xD3 , 0xD8 , 0xB4 , 0x85 , 0xA3 , 0x6B , 0x25 ) are test vectors: the tests check them against both the driver's CRC and a separately written model CRC. A reply is checked for the sync nibble, the master address, the requested register and the CRC. Writes and the interface counter ¶ A write has no reply. Each accepted write increments IFCNT (page 33), so Verify::Counter reads IFCNT and checks it counted the write. Enable() compares IFCNT with the number of writes the driver sent: a lost write means a register the driver thinks it wrote is still at its reset value, and Enable() quiesces the chip and returns VerifyFailed . Writes are not retried; reads are retried twice ( kUartReadRetries ), because a read has no side effect. SENDDELAY and timeouts ¶ The reply starts after SENDDELAY times 8 bit times (default 8; 0 and 1 are equal; at least 2 with several nodes). The port's timeout_us is that delay plus a margin of 64 bit times at the declared baud (A32). Several nodes ¶ // Two chips on one line: each driver object has its own node address. tmc5160 :: Error StartTwoNodes ( MyUartPort & port ) { tmc5160 :: Config config = tmc5160 :: MakeConfig ( tmc5160 :: Motor {. rated_rms_ma = 1000 , . coil_resistance_mohm = 6000 }, tmc5160 :: Board {. rsense_mohm = 100 , . supply_mv = 24'000 }); config . uart . multi_node = true ; // addresses 0 to 254 are valid config . uart . send_delay = 4 ; // the reply waits 4 * 8 bit times: needed with several nodes tmc5160 :: Config second = config ; config . uart . node = 1 ; second . uart . node = 2 ; static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyUartPort > first_motor ( port , config ); static tmc5160 :: TMC5160 < MyUartPort > second_motor ( port , second ); if ( auto r = first_motor . EnsureInitialized (); ! r ) { return r . error ; } return second_motor . EnsureInitialized (). error ; } NODEADDR is 0 to 253; the chain procedure on page 29 programs node 254 for the first chip, so multi_node allows 254 (A31). ProgramNode(from, to, nao_level) writes NODECONF through the old address and sets the NAO output that opens the next chip's addressing. After it the driver follows the chip to its new address. UART needs SPI_MODE and SD_MODE low; SWP carries the signal and SWN can stay open. Hardware notes ¶ The two UART pins are DIAG1_SWP and DIAG0_SWN, so DIAG outputs are not available in UART mode. With a shared transmit and receive wire the port must read and drop the echo of its own bytes ( Porting ).
